papers.title: A COMPREHENSIVE BENCHMARK OF SOURCE-FREE UNIVERSAL DOMAIN ADAPTATION ON TIME SERIES REPRESENTATIONS
papers.abstract: Source-Free Universal Domain Adaptation (SF-UniDA) extends Universal Domain Adaptation by removing access to source data at adaptation time while still handling label-set mismatches between domains. Despite growing interest in this setting for image data, no benchmark exists for time series, which are more challenging. We present the first SF-UniDA benchmark on time series. In addition, we provide the first study of pretrained foundation models as feature extractors for time series domain adaptation. In this context, we identify a critical and previously underexplored limitation of all existing SF-UniDA methods: the inference threshold for unknown-sample rejection is highly sensitive. We address this by proposing a plug-in auto-thresholding module that can be integrated into any SF-UniDA method. Experiments on three well-known time series datasets confirm the suitability of this module. They also highlight that foundation models do not systematically outperform classical backbones and that SF-UniDA tailored for time series is yet to be developed.

papers.title: Adaptive Filtering of the KV Cache: Diagnosing and Correcting Structural-Role Bias in LLM Inference
papers.abstract: Attention-based KV cache eviction (H2O and its descendants) compresses the memory-constrained state of a long-context model by ranking tokens on accumulated attention mass, treated here as signal energy, and keeping the heaviest. On schema-dense input streams such as nested JSON, this score acts as a non-stationary filter that disproportionately retains noise: a non-content sink role (delimiters or whitespace) carries an order of magnitude more energy than any content role, and structural KEY tokens are over-retained at roughly $1.8\times$ the rate of the answer-carrying VALUE tokens, collapsing exact-match accuracy from 88\% to 0\% at a 5\% budget as the signal-to-noise ratio of the retained state degrades. A counterfactual experiment establishes that suppressing KEY tokens is the best deployable filter. Our retraining-free, role-conditional allocation over SnapKV's windowed score, governed by a single hyperparameter, closes 63--98\% of the H2O gap at sub-20\% budgets and, at moderate budgets, exceeds full-budget accuracy by acting as an implicit denoiser. A 15\,MB linear role probe provides a low-latency feature extractor for resource-constrained inference.

papers.title: Commutator-Based Symmetry Analysis Identifies Replaceable Attention Heads in Transformers
papers.abstract: We propose a group-theoretic diagnostic for transformer attention based on commutator norms with finite permutation groups. The permutation-baseline-normalized commutator residual $\delta_{\mathrm{norm}}$ measures whether a head's average attention matrix commutes with a candidate group more than a random matrix would, computed from attention statistics alone with no labels and no probing classifier. On the GPT-2 family, heads partition cleanly into a positional class ($\delta_{\mathrm{norm}} < 0.5$, approximately circulant) and a content class ($\delta_{\mathrm{norm}} > 0.9$). The classification is actionable and its value is structural: replacing positional heads with a fixed causal circulant pattern is functionally exact away from the class boundary (perplexity ratios 0.997 to 1.006 for the strongest heads on every GPT-2 size, improving on GPT-2 Large; boundary heads at $\delta_{\mathrm{norm}} > 0.44$ cost up to 2.5\% on the two smallest models) at 3.2\% attention-FLOP savings and zero added parameters, while uniform substitution of content heads degrades perplexity by up to 89\%. Because the commutator ranking is orthogonal to ablation-based importance (0\% top-20 overlap), it composes with deletion-based pruning: the combination affects 19\% of heads at a 0.980 perplexity ratio and 17\% attention-FLOP savings, with the improvement attributable entirely to the deletion component. The classification is stable under fine-tuning and extends qualitatively across architectures: learned-absolute (OPT), rotary (Pythia, Phi-3, Gemma-2), and bidirectional (BERT, ModernBERT) models all exhibit the positional class. Sensitivity analyses show the positional census depends on the calibration corpus and on fine-tuning only at the class boundary.

papers.title: ECG Foundation Model Features Improve Atrial Fibrillation Alarm Precision in Intensive Care Monitoring
papers.abstract:
Atrial fibrillation (AF) alarms generated by intensive care unit bed-
side monitors are designed to be sensitive, but false alarms remain
common and contribute to alarm fatigue. We evaluated whether
ECG foundation model (ECG-FM) embeddings improve discrimi-
nation of true AF alarms from AF-mimicking false alarms compared
with engineered ECG features. Clinicians annotated 711 AF alarms
with matched 30-second ECG waveforms, of which 159 (22.4%)
were false alarms. We compared engineered ECG features, ECG-
FM embeddings, and demographic features using stratified group
cross-validation. ECG-FM achieved the best performance, with area
under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUROC) of 0.903
and area under the precision-recall curve of 0.963. At approximately
90% sensitivity, ECG-FM increased positive predictive value from
the baseline alarm precision of 0.776 to 0.945 and suppressed 130 of
159 false alarms. These findings suggest that ECG foundation model
representations can substantially improve AF alarm precision while
preserving high sensitivity.

papers.title: GEOMETRY-AWARE GRAPH CONSTRUCTION VIA ADAPTIVE SPECTRAL BANDWIDTH CONTROL
papers.abstract:
Kernelized graph methods — spectral clustering, diffusion maps,
and sparse kernel-regression graphs — that use Gaussian kernels depend on the choice of Gaussian bandwidth $\sigma$, which governs the spectral character
of the local kernel operator.

When $\sigma$ is too small, the kernel overestimates local complexity
and treats each sample as an independent direction; when $\sigma$ is
too large, the kernel collapses multiple directions together, the
condition number diverges, and all geometric discrimination is lost.
We propose a choice of scale to make the spectral complexity of the kernel consistent with the intrinsic complexity
of the underlying manifold.

We propose a per-node bandwidth criterion that operationalizes this
principle by jointly matching the kernel's effective rank to the local intrinsic dimension estimated via minimum spanning tree, anchoring the search in the manifold-consistent log-log scaling regime.

We evaluate SSL embeddings from six encoders on CIFAR-100, showing that adaptive bandwidth consistently improves leave-one-out (LOO) classification and label propagation (LP) accuracy over fixed-bandwidth methods and competing adaptive methods.

papers.title: Ghost Features and Spooky Transfer Learning for Hypercomplex-Valued Neural Networks
papers.abstract: Hypercomplex numbers extend the concept of complex numbers by introducing additional imaginary components. Besides increasing dimensionality, operations on the imaginary parts provide algebraic and geometrical properties that can be beneficial for solving machine learning problems. In this paper, we show how to create hypercomplex-valued neural network layers where the real part corresponds to the output of a traditional real-valued layer. The additional imaginary parts of these hypercomplex-valued layers produce what we call "ghost features,'' which contain enhanced information that is not present in the output of the real-valued layer. Moreover, ghost features can be effectively integrated into a trained neural network through a process we refer to as ``spooky transfer learning.'' This approach allows us to harness the richness of ghost features, leading to more efficient neural networks. The source code and Jupyter Notebook are available at https://github.com/mevalle/v-nets/.

papers.title: Jacobi-Anger Method for Deterministic Initialization in Implicit Neural Representation
papers.abstract: Existing implicit neural representation (INR) approaches suffer from stochastic initialization that does not guarantee consistent or high-quality performance across runs, with variations reaching more than 2.5 dB ($\sim$78\%) in image regression. This variation is problematic for scientific computing and simulation, where result reproducibility is crucial. To address this problem, we present Jacobi-Anger Sinusoidal Representation Network (JA-SIREN), a deterministic initialization scheme for sinusoidal networks grounded in classical spectral analysis. By computing the Discrete Sine Transform (DST) of the target signal and leveraging the Jacobi-Anger expansion, we derive deterministic weights for a two-layer sinusoidal MLP that analytically match the network's initial spectral response to the target signal. On the Kodak dataset, JA-SIREN achieves a mean PSNR of 67.18 dB, a 21.30 dB improvement over the best baseline. This is achieved with zero run-to-run variance, confirming that spectrally-informed initialization is a more effective and reproducible alternative to stochastic initialization for sinusoidal INRs.

papers.title: Learning with Volterra Neural Networks: A System Theoretic Perspective
papers.abstract: Higher-order interaction components are important for signal, image, and video modeling, but explicit high-order operators often suffer from rapidly increasing parameter and computational costs. This paper presents kVNN, a learnable kernelized Volterra Neural operator for compact higher-order filtering. The motivation is to use kernelization to improve the efficiency of Volterra-type neural operators while providing a structured interpretation of their higher-order components. The proposed formulation combines the order-wise structure of Volterra filtering with learnable polynomial-kernel atoms, allowing different interaction orders to be represented by separate learnable centers and coefficients. This order-decoupled representation avoids explicit high-order tensor parameterization and can be implemented as a CNN-compatible layer. Experiments on representative vision tasks show that kVNN achieves a favorable accuracy--efficiency trade-off.

papers.title: MODEL-AGNOSTIC RETRIEVAL-AUGMENTED EXTENDED FORECASTING FOR TIME SERIES
papers.abstract:
Time series forecasting with pretrained foundation models has demonstrated strong zero-shot capabilities. However, achieving optimal performance on time series with short or negligible historical data in domain-specific applications typically requires adaptation via either fine-tuning or RAG. While fine-tuning is effective, it incurs substantial computational costs. This work explores RAG within univariate
time series (Retrieval Augmented Generation) as a more efficient alternative, in particular RAF (Retrieval Augmented Forecasting), and introduces RAEF (Retrieval-Augmented Extended Forecasting), a model-agnostic method built upon RAF.
RAEF incorporates key refinements to the retrieval and aggregation mechanisms: (1) direct retrieval in input-space rather than embedding-space, reducing inference overhead, and (2) concatenation-based aggregation that preserves temporal structure instead of averaging. Empirical evaluation across multiple benchmark datasets demonstrates that RAEF outperforms RAF in both accuracy and inference overhead. Furthermore, comprehensive comparisons with zero-shot and fine-tuned foundation models show that RAEF achieves competitive or superior performance to fine-tuning while avoiding its computational burden, establishing it as a practical and scalable approach for domain adaptation in time series forecasting.

papers.title: Neural Compression for Unsupervised Bayesian Despeckling
papers.abstract:
Multiplicative noise, commonly referred to as speckle noise, is a fundamental limitation in coherent imaging systems such as Synthetic Aperture Radar (SAR) and digital holography. In this paper, we study Bayesian Despeckling via Quantized Maximum A Posteriori (BD-QMAP), an image despeckling method that combines a likelihood-based measurement fidelity term with a source-adaptive regularizer. The regularizer is determined by source-dependent weights that capture the information content of the underlying source, making accurate and efficient weight estimation central to the method.

We theoretically characterize the despeckling performance of BD-QMAP for piecewise-constant sources. We then introduce a neural data-compression approach for estimating the required source weights from image patches. The resulting framework learns a compact representation of source statistics using a neural compression network trained on image patches and applies the learned model within BD-QMAP. Experiments show that the proposed method achieves performance comparable to state-of-the-art block-matching methods and remains competitive with supervised end-to-end deep learning approaches, while relying only on statistics learned from $8\times 8$ image patches.

papers.title: PHYSICS-AUGMENTED GRAPH TRANSFORMERS FOR PATCH-ANTENNA FORWARD AND INVERSE DESIGN
papers.abstract: Full-wave electromagnetic (EM) simulation enables accurate patch-antenna analysis but is too slow for large-scale forward prediction and inverse design. We present a mesh-native, physics-augmented graph-learning framework that treats radiation-pattern prediction as signal reconstruction on an irregular surface mesh. For the forward problem, a GPS graph transformer is trained with Physics-Augmented Intermediate Supervision (PAIS), an auxiliary node-level objective that predicts complex surface currents, the physical intermediate linking geometry to radiation. PAIS improves multiple GNN backbones at no inference-time cost, while shuffled-current and non-physical controls show the gain comes from physical correspondence. Direction-conditioned decoding and a differentiable radiation-integral consistency loss further exploit this structure. On an 80,000-sample CST benchmark, GPS+PAIS reaches MSE 0.17 / PSNR 19.67, generalizes to a PCA split, and transfers zero-shot to canonical patches. For inverse design, surrogate-filtered diffusion beats nearest-neighbor retrieval by 32\% relative MSE.

papers.title: PITCH-CLASS STEERING FOR DIFFUSION-BASED MUSIC GENERATION VIA LATENT-SPACE PROBES
papers.abstract: Recent work on controllable music generation has focused on autoregressive models, leaving diffusion-based systems comparatively underexplored. We present a lightweight method for steering the pitch content of audio produced by Stable Audio Open, a latent diffusion model for music synthesis. A small convolutional probe containing approximately 125k parameters is trained to decode frame-level pitch-class activations from the model’s variational autoencoder latent space, using paired audio and MIDI data. At inference time, the frozen probe serves as a differentiable loss function: its gradient with respect to the denoising latent is used to nudge generation toward a user-specified pitch-class sequence, requiring no retraining or architectural modification of the base model. Across 27 evaluation trials spanning 9 text prompts and 3 target melodies, probe-guided generation increases melodic coherence by $2.4\times$ over the unguided baseline ($p < 10^{-5}$, Wilcoxon signed-rank test), demonstrating that musically meaningful structure is both recoverable and steerable in diffusion-based music latent spaces.

papers.title: PROBABILISTIC LOW-RANK ADAPTATION OF LARGE LANGUAGE MODELS VIA MOMENT PROPAGATION
papers.abstract: Parameter-efficient fine-tuning (PEFT) enables large language models to adapt to downstream tasks by updating only a small set of adapter parameters. However, conventional PEFT methods, such as low-rank adaptation (LoRA), learn deterministic point estimates and therefore provide limited information about predictive uncertainty, often leading to overconfident predictions. Bayesian PEFT methods address this limitation by placing distributions over adapter parameters, but many practical approaches approximate uncertainty through local perturbations and single-sample posterior estimation. As a result, they underestimate epistemic uncertainty, leading to poorly calibrated predictions and causing models to remain overconfident despite their Bayesian formulation. To address these shortcomings, we propose a novel Bayesian fine-tuning framework for low-rank adapters in which uncertainty is represented as a learnable quantity that is propagated jointly with the mean through the down-projection LoRA weights via moment propagation. This allows the model to capture non-local epistemic uncertainty in the adapter parameters, rather than treating it as isolated additive noise at each layer. Experiments on commonsense reasoning and question-answering benchmarks demonstrate improved calibration and uncertainty estimation while maintaining competitive task performance, suggesting that probabilistic adapters can make PEFT more reliable for large language models.

papers.title: Target Detection via Denoising Score Matching
papers.abstract:
We study adaptive target detection in unknown and possibly non-Gaussian background clutter using target-free secondary data. We take a hybrid model-based and data-driven approach. Learning is used to model the background, while the detector and its normalization are kept in the form prescribed by classical detection theory. Our focus is on the locally most powerful (LMP) detector that depends on the background only through its score function and a few score moments. We exploit this structure by estimating the background characteristics with denoising score matching (DSM) and plugging the estimate into the detector. This separation allows a single learned background model to be reused across target signatures. In the affine Gaussian case, the proposed method reduces to a regularized adaptive matched filter, which explains its advantages in finite sample regimes. We also develop a spatially adaptive extension that improves accuracy while maintaining empirical constant false alarm rate (CFAR) calibration in spatially varying environments.
Experiments on three real hyperspectral scenes illustrate the advantages of the proposed detectors with respect to Gaussian, Gaussian mixture, learned Rao, and recent deep learning baselines.

papers.title: Tiny Flow Matching: Constrained Low-Rank OT-CFM for Deployable Ergodic UAV Coverage
papers.abstract: Learned pushforward maps based on optimal-transport conditional flow matching (OT-CFM) generate ergodic UAV trajectories whose long-run occupancy matches a prescribed spatial density. However, the learned velocity field must be repeatedly evaluated during ODE integration, making deployment costly on edge and embedded platforms. This paper adapts constrained low-rank training to OT-CFM trajectory generators. Selected velocity-network layers are trained with auxiliary rank-constrained variables and a quadratic coupling penalty, then converted into explicit factorized layers by hard SVD truncation. We also give a stability bound showing that uniform approximation of the dense velocity field controls the deviation between dense and factorized flow maps and their induced long-run occupancy averages. We evaluate the method against Dense OT-CFM and Naive SVD on the Milano UAV benchmark and six target distributions, including synthetic and real-world datasets. On Milano, rank-4 constrained LR OT-CFM retains $99.45\%$ of the Dense OT-CFM coverage correlation while using only $3.77\%$ of the selected-layer parameter count; Naive SVD retains only $55.78\%$. Across datasets, moderate ranks preserve most dense-model coverage, while the rank-4 factorized model reduces FP32 size from $0.7588$ MB to $0.0323$ MB and MACs per velocity evaluation from $197{,}888$ to $7{,}437$.

papers.title: GENERALIZING SUPERVISED CONTRASTIVE LEARNING: A PROJECTION PERSPECTIVE
papers.abstract: Supervised contrastive (SupCon) learning is widely used for label-aware representation learning, but its connection to mutual information (MI) is less understood than that of self-supervised InfoNCE. In addition, SupCon implicitly represents each class by the centroid of same-class embeddings, which can be fragile under label noise or heterogeneous class structure. We introduce ProjNCE, a projection-based generalization of InfoNCE and SupCon that maps class labels into the embedding space using positive and negative projection functions. With an adjustment term for negative pairs, ProjNCE yields a valid lower bound on the MI between features and labels, while also enabling flexible class projections such as orthogonal, median, and learnable MLP projections. Experiments on image and audio benchmarks, including noisy-label settings, show that ProjNCE consistently improves over SupCon and strong supervised contrastive baselines. These results highlight projection design and MI-preserving correction as effective tools for supervised contrastive learning.

papers.title: Causal-Reliability-Aware State Estimation: Learning Admissible Representations under Partial Observability
papers.abstract: State estimators are often selected by reconstruction error, but lower reconstruction error does not necessarily imply reliable causal discovery. In partially observed dynamical systems, smoothing can leak future information into past state proxies and inflate false causal edges. This paper studies which estimated-state representations are admissible for causal graph recovery. We identify two independent requirements: self-consistency, so the proxy follows a white-residual recursion readable by temporal causal backends, and coordinate alignment, so the recovered graph corresponds to the physical state coordinates rather than a rotated latent basis. Under whitening, the recovery bias decomposes into a readability term and a physical-coordinate term, separating future-innovation leakage from alignment error. We introduce SCEM, a firewall architecture that separates a strictly forward causal channel used for graph extraction from a bidirectional residual channel used only for reconstruction. In well-specified linear-Gaussian systems, the causal channel reduces to the Kalman filter, preserving filter-grade causal reliability while the residual channel recovers smoother-grade reconstruction. Symbolic witnesses, finite-sample ablations, capacity sweeps, and real-topology simulator benchmarks validate the two admissibility conditions and show the failure modes caused by removing either the firewall or coordinate alignment.

papers.title: Efficient Federated Learning via Low-Rank Distributed Auto-Differentiation
papers.abstract: Although distributed machine learning has opened many new and exciting research frontiers, the fragmentation of models and data across machines, nodes, and sites still results in considerable communication overhead, thereby impeding reliable training in real-world contexts. The focus on gradients as the primary shared statistic during training has spurred a number of intuitive distributed deep learning algorithms; however, gradient-centric training of large deep neural networks (DNNs) tends to be communication-heavy, often requiring additional adaptations such as sparsity constraints and quantization. We introduce an innovative, communication-friendly approach to training distributed DNNs that leverages the product structure of the gradient revealed by the mechanics of auto-differentiation. The exposed structure of the gradient suggests a new class of distributed learning algorithms that are naturally communication-efficient. Our approach, called rank-distributed auto-differentiation (rank-dAD), builds off a marriage of rank-based compression and the innate structure of the gradient as a product.

papers.title: Fed-ETF: Adaptive and Robust Federated Learning under Data Heterogeneity and Byzantine Attacks
papers.abstract:
We propose Fed-ETF, a Byzantine-robust federated learning framework that addresses the dual challenges of data heterogeneity and adversarial client behaviors. Our approach introduces a novel trust-based aggregation mechanism and adaptive learning rates to improve global model robustness and performance. Specifically, each client’s contribution is evaluated using a trust score; a similarity-based metric computed via cosine similarity between a client’s update and a reference update derived from a trusted dataset. These scores are iteratively updated and used to filter out unreliable clients and reweight contributions during aggregation through a Trust Score Filtering mechanism. 
To address the client drift issue in heterogeneous environments and stabilize training, we incorporate an Exponential Moving Average-based adaptive learning rate strategy that dynamically adjusts client-side learning rates in proportion to their trust scores. 
Theoretically, we provide convergence guarantees under convex and smooth loss conditions, quantifying the impact of the trust score mechanism and discard rate on model performance. Empirical evaluations on non-IID data and under multiple adversarial scenarios demonstrate that Fed-ETF significantly outperforms existing methods.

papers.title: Personalized Federated Learning through Global Knowledge Distillation and Local Head Adaptation

authors.name: José Mairton Barros da Silva Júnior

papers.abstract: Statistical heterogeneity limits federated learning when a single global classifier cannot represent client-specific label distributions. In this work, we propose Personalized Federated Knowledge Distillation with Head Adaptation (pFedKDH), which aggregates only the shared backbone, keeps persistent client-specific heads, and uses a recalibrated global head as a teacher during local training. Across MNIST, Fashion-MNIST, CIFAR10, and CIFAR100 under class-wise Dirichlet partitions, pFedKDH obtains the best accuracy in most settings, with accuracy gaps up to 37.67\% over the weakest baseline and consistently low standard deviation across repetitions. Component-wise diagnostics and convergence results support the role of persistent heads and distillation-guided local optimization under label-skewed data.

papers.title: Rank-Based Federated Markov Blanket Aggregation for Survival Prediction from Non-IID Head and Neck Cancer Cohorts
papers.abstract: Federated learning enables multi-institutional model development without direct exchange of patient-level data, but most healthcare applications focus on distributed model optimization rather than federated feature discovery. We propose a rank-based federated Markov blanket aggregation framework for two-year survival prediction in head and neck cancer under non-identically distributed clinical data. A public cohort of 3,346 patients was used, yielding a 2,994-patient analysis dataset after excluding incomplete cases. Patients were temporally split into development ($n=2{,}174$) and locked temporal test ($n=820$) sets. The development set was partitioned into five heterogeneous simulated clients. Each client independently performed bootstrapped Bayesian-network Markov blanket discovery, after which feature-level summaries were aggregated using union, voting, stability-weighted, and Borda rank-based consensus strategies. Rank-Borda Top-8 selected a compact feature set and achieved a temporal test AUC of 0.647, C-index of 0.772, and significant Kaplan--Meier risk separation ($p<0.001$), with performance comparable to less restrictive MB-derived baselines. These results suggest that rank-based aggregation can provide compact, interpretable feature sets for federated survival prediction under heterogeneous clinical distributions while preserving data locality.

papers.title: Retain-Free Machine Unlearning for Speech Emotion Recognition
papers.abstract: Speech Emotion Recognition (SER) infers a speaker's emotional state from speech and is increasingly deployed in human-computer interaction, education, and healthcare. Because speech also carries sensitive personal information, speakers may ask that some of their recordings be deleted, which requires removing the influence of those samples from an already trained SER model. Most machine unlearning methods can meet this request only with access to the remaining training data alongside the samples to be forgotten; this is impractical when the remaining data cannot be redistributed or has itself been deleted, and it adds storage and computation as the data grows. To this end, we propose a retain-free unlearning method that updates a pre-trained SER model using only the forget set. Our key idea is to synthesise adversarial samples from the forget set as a surrogate for the unavailable remaining data, and to constrain each parameter update by its estimated importance so that forgetting does not erase general knowledge. The experiments over several emotional-speech corpora and self-supervised backbones show that our method drives forget-set performance down to near chance while retaining much of the model's utility on the remaining and unseen-speaker data, narrowing the gap to methods that rely on the remaining set.

papers.title: The Impact of Validation Strategies on AI Models for Repeated-Measures Biomarkers: A Tuberculosis Case Study
papers.abstract:
Biomarkers are increasingly measured repeatedly for each individual through mobile, wearable, and remote-monitoring technologies, producing clustered data in which several records belong to the same subject. How such data are partitioned for validation strongly affects the apparent performance of the resulting AI models, yet this choice is often treated as a technical detail. We demonstrate this effect for cough-based tuberculosis (TB) screening, using the multi-country CODA TB DREAM dataset to contrast two validation strategies. Record-wise (k-fold) validation randomly partitions all records regardless of subject identity, while subject-wise validation holds out all data from an individual entirely to test generalization to new subjects.
We assess the effect of each strategy on accuracy, sensitivity, specificity, and ROC~AUC for a linear model (Logistic Regression) and a non-linear ensemble (XGBoost). Our findings show that the choice of validation scheme markedly influences estimated performance. For XGBoost, record-wise validation reaches a near-perfect test ROC AUC of 1.00 and accuracy of 0.99, which fall to 0.83 and 0.66 under subject-wise evaluation, because record-wise splitting can reward subject recognition rather than disease detection.
Based on these results, we provide recommendations for validating repeated-measures biomarker models, illustrated for TB triage.

papers.title: A Deep Learning Framework for Joint AMC, Demodulation, and SNR Estimation in Radar-Centric ISAC Systems
papers.abstract: Modern Integrated Sensing and Communication (ISAC) systems are gaining interest for next-generation wireless applications, yet their potential in electronic-warfare-oriented ISAC (EW-ISAC) remains underexplored. This paper proposes PRI-LFM-PM, a dual-functional waveform combining pulse repetition interval (PRI), linear frequency modulation (LFM), and phase modulation (PM) for joint sensing and communication in EW-ISAC. Automatic Modulation Classification (AMC) is the primary task, with bitstream demodulation and Signal-to-Noise Ratio (SNR) estimation as auxiliary tasks. A Unified Multi-Task AMC (UMT-AMC) framework with self-verification and self-correction mechanisms is introduced to jointly address these objectives. By unifying the three tasks in a single architecture, the model enables shared representation learning and improves performance across all tasks. Extensive experiments on five datasets, including RML2016.10a, RML2016.10b, PRI-LFM, PRI-LFM-CPM, and PRI-LFM-PM, demonstrate that the proposed model either outperforms state-of-the-art (SOTA) methods or achieves comparable performance under varying SNR conditions. The source code is available at https://anonymous.4open.science/r/UMTAMC_EWISAC-EA7E.

papers.title: Comparative Analysis of Machine Learning Classifiers for Magnetometer-Based Silent Speech Recognition: Sensor Axis Ablation and Noise Robustness
papers.abstract:
Silent speech interfaces (SSIs) require robust signal classifiers capable of handling sensor noise and placement variability in wearable settings. This paper presents a controlled comparative study of machine learning classifiers (Random Forest (RF), 1D-CNN, and Bidirectional LSTM (BiLSTM)) applied to magnetometer-based articulatory tracking, evaluated against a Dynamic Time Warping (DTW) baseline. Using two three-axis TLV493D magnetometers mounted on a lightweight headset frame tracking three pairs of external NdFeB disc magnets across the lips, we collect 1,500 recordings across a 10-word vocabulary under controlled conditions. The controlled
single-subject design isolates classifier behaviour from inter-subject
articulatory variability, enabling direct attribution of performance
differences to model architecture. Our study makes three contributions to classifier selection for this sensing modality. First, a systematic ablation over all 62 non-trivial axis subsets reveals that the vertical jaw axis (Z) alone achieves 80.0\% accuracy, while an optimized 2-axis configuration ($S_{2X} + S_{2Z}$) retains 84.0\% accuracy, reducing active channels by 67\%. Second, a six-condition noise robustness analysis reveals complementary classifier strengths: RF is structurally immune to signal offset through translation-invariant features; BiLSTM maintains performance within 0.3 percentage points under 30\% impulse corruption. Third, DTW, while competitive offline, is shown to be fundamentally incompatible with cross-session deployment due to its dependence on absolute signal values. These findings provide evidence-based classifier selection guidance for future magnetometer-based SSI development.

papers.title: CPIP- A Representation Learning for RF Signals
papers.abstract:
Many radar machine learning (ML) tasks require reasoning jointly over received I/Q signals and the pulse descriptor word (PDW) parameters that characterize them. However, today’s RF learning pipelines treat these two modalities independently. We propose Contrastive PDW–I/Q Pre-Training (CPIP), a dual-encoder framework that learns a shared latent space for I/Q signals and their associated PDW parameters. To ensure that the I/Q representations contain features relevant to each parameter in the full PDW vector, CPIP trains on parameter-wise masked PDW views, aligning each I/Q sample with individual pulse attributes in isolation. Our experiments show that CPIP embeddings (i) form interpretable clusters, influenced by time-of-arrival, pulse width, and bandwidth, (ii) support PDW parameter regression that, after fine-
tuning, outperforms existing I/Q-based regression methods, and (iii) can be used to evaluate conditional fidelity of generative models as CPIP provides a joint feature space sensitive to conditional mismatch.

papers.title: Dynamic Clustering for Cross-Segment Permutation Alignment in Long Speech Separation
papers.abstract: Long speech separation typically employs a segment-separation-stitch paradigm where recordings are divided into short segments, processed independently, and stitched together. Its challenge lies in predicting cross-segment permutations. This paper proposes a training-free dynamic clustering approach for cross-segment permutation alignment using speaker embedding reference pools. The method predicts the permutation using the cosine similarity between current segment embeddings and the reference pools. The approach updates reference pools by retaining the most representative speaker embeddings based on their overall cosine similarity with existing references. As a plug-and-play post-processing module compatible with existing separation models, the proposed method demonstrates superior performance compared to existing methods on dense and sparse long speech scenarios, particularly in challenging sparse scenarios with extended utterance gaps, and further shows robustness to speaker count estimation errors in unknown speaker count scenarios.

papers.title: How Convex-Combination Decoder Training Shapes Latent Adaptive Filter Dynamics
papers.abstract: Latent adaptive filters constrain adaptive filter coefficients to lie in the range of a learned decoder, enabling low-dimensional adaptation for time-varying systems with structured coefficient sets. This paper uses convex-combination decoder training to study how decoder objectives shape latent adaptive filter dynamics. We compare reconstruction-only training with mixup and simplicial regularization under fixed online update rules, treating these losses as probes of the tradeoff between representing measured coefficient vectors and representing intermediate states encountered during adaptation. System-identification experiments with abrupt changes and source-tracking experiments on simulated and measured acoustic impulse responses show that convex-combination losses can improve mean transient adaptation and tracking, but can also increase steady-state error, reflecting the familiar tradeoff between convergence and steady-state accuracy. The results suggest that these benefits are not explained by interpolation between impulse responses alone; rather, they arise partly from improved decoder behavior on intermediate coefficient-space states encountered during adaptation, while their costs reflect reduced accuracy on the original coefficient manifold.

papers.title: LEARNING FROM OBSERVATIONAL VARIABILITY: PHYSICALLY-GROUNDED CONTRASTIVE LEARNING FOR SLITLESS SPECTROSCOPY
papers.abstract: Ground-based satellite identification in Space Domain Awareness (SDA) often relies on slitless spectroscopy, but highly variable observation conditions and noisy spectra complicate robust classification. While contrastive learning improves spectral identification, current methods depend heavily on artificial data augmentations. We introduce a novel contrastive learning framework that leverages naturally occurring spectral variations, driven by physical changes in illumination and viewing geometry, as alternative training views. Evaluated on real ground-based observations, this data-driven approach outperforms standard augmentation-only methods in a difficult downstream satellite identification tasks.

papers.title: PathogenIQ: An End-to-End Machine Learning Pipeline for Metagenomic Wastewater Surveillance
papers.abstract:
Metagenomic sequencing-based biosurveillance provides population-level
pathogen monitoring without individual testing, but existing bioinformatics
pipelines lack integrated machine learning for risk stratification, temporal
outbreak detection, and automated alerting. We present \textit{PathogenIQ},
a modular, open-source, end-to-end pipeline that ingests Kraken2 taxonomic
reports and integrates a false-discovery-rate (FDR)-corrected Spearman
co-occurrence graph with stochastic block model (SBM) community detection, a multi-signal composite risk scorer combining curated pathogen
abundance weights, community context, and isolation-forest-based
cohort-relative anomaly (novelty) detection, cumulative sum (CUSUM)
changepoint and Mann-Kendall trend analysis, and a real-time web
dashboard with Slack/email alerting.
On 60 real wastewater samples ($\sim$30-week site-207 series),
PathogenIQ classifies 55 runs as MODERATE and 5 as HIGH, where an
abundance-only threshold raises none; we show this divergence reflects
PathogenIQ's operational decision logic (a fixed community-context
offset and a cohort-recalibrated direct-detection rule supplying the
threshold margin) rather than superior raw detection. The CUSUM layer
transiently crosses its decision boundary ($C_t=4.54$ vs. $h=4.0$) around
week 20 before receding to baseline, capturing a transient risk excursion.
On six controlled synthetic scenarios ($N=52$), the abundance-driven
pathway reaches Sensitivity=98.8\%, F1=99.3\% with zero false positives
(FAR=0.0\% across 10 seeds), a 50-point FAR reduction over a na\"{i}ve
threshold, while community and novelty signals add interpretable context
without changing binary alert decisions. PathogenIQ's central contribution is this end-to-end integration: an open-source system to carry raw Kraken2 reports through to a deployable alerting dashboard, replacing manual report-by-report review with continuous automated surveillance.

papers.title: Root Selection and Structured Neural Reception for Index-Modulated OCDM ISAC with Zadoff--Chu Sensing
papers.abstract: Inactive resources in index-modulated orthogonal chirp division multiplexing (IM-OCDM) provide a natural means of embedding a deterministic sensing component without occupying additional communication resources. However, inserting a Zadoff--Chu (ZC)-derived component in the inactive subchirps changes both the Fresnel-domain waveform structure and the associated detection problem. In particular, the transmitted component is the local discrete Fresnel transform (DFnT) image of the ZC sequence rather than the temporal constant-amplitude zero-autocorrelation waveform, thereby coupling EISL-oriented root selection to communication recovery. We study this interaction for $(N,g,n_c)=(64,16,4)$ and propose CNN-TransISAC, a structured receiver that combines circular convolutional feature extraction, Transformer-based context modeling, power-ratio and SNR conditioning, auxiliary COMM/RADAR supervision, support-margin regularization, and group-wise maximum a posteriori (MAP) projection onto the valid index-modulation alphabet. Under Rayleigh fading with imperfect channel state information (CSI), the communication-favored $\mathrm{PR}=-3$ dB configuration achieves a BER below $1%$ for $k=2$ and about $2%$ for $k=3$ at $20$ dB. Internal diagnostics further indicate that COMM/RADAR structure emerges before MAP projection. These results support joint ZC-root and receiver design in the evaluated IM-OCDM regime without implying a universal root-selection rule.

papers.title: SonoBite: Ultrasound Sensing for Smartphone-based Food Recognition
papers.abstract: Continuous dietary monitoring is important for preventive healthcare and personalized nutrition management, yet existing food recognition systems often rely on wearable devices or camera-based sensing that limit usability and raise privacy concerns. In this paper, we present SonoBite, a smartphone-based food recognition system using active ultrasound acoustic sensing and deep learning. SonoBite transforms commodity smartphones into active sensing platforms by emitting inaudible ultrasound chirps and analyzing chewing-induced signal reflections during food consumption. The reflected signals are converted into STFT spectrograms and processed using a deep neural network trained with domain generalization for robust food recognition. We evaluate SonoBite through extensive experiments involving 20 participants across diverse real-world environments. Results show that SonoBite improves the state-of-the-art baseline by 7\% accuracy while maintaining robustness across heterogeneous users, devices, sensing distances, and environmental conditions. Our study demonstrates the feasibility of privacy-preserving dietary sensing using ubiquitous mobile devices.

papers.title: Wigner--Ville Distribution Slice Spectra for Early Anomaly-Onset Detection in High-Voltage Transmission-Grid Waveforms
papers.abstract: Early disturbance recognition in power systems is commonly evaluated as offline record-level classification, although practical monitoring requires sequential decisions from evolving waveform windows. This paper presents a Wigner-Ville Distribution Slice (WVDS) representation for early anomaly-onset detection in high-voltage grid waveforms. Instead of treating Wigner-Ville distribution cross terms only as artifacts to be suppressed, the study uses their midpoint interaction behavior as part of a full-vector time-frequency representation. Each 128-sample voltage window is transformed into a 128-dimensional WVDS spectrum and evaluated without manual fault-frequency selection. A baseline-normalized deviation (BND) detector is combined with WVDS and compared with the BND of Fast Fourier Transform (FFT-BND), raw-signal autoencoders, FFT autoencoders, and WVDS autoencoders under a common threshold and sequential persistence rule. A synthetic autoencoder--clustering teacher filters RTE voltage fault records to retain examples that begin normally and later transition to anomalous behavior. The results show that FFT-BND provides the highest detection sensitivity, whereas WVDS-BND gives the most conservative low-false-alarm operating point, reducing record-level pre-onset false alarms to 0.69\%. The autoencoder results show a similar trend that WVDS-based reconstruction reduces false alarms relative to FFT-based reconstruction, although with more missed detections. These findings indicate that retained WVD cross-term structure can provide a selective representation for sequential grid-waveform anomaly monitoring.

papers.title: A 2-Block Architecture for Real-Time EEG Gait Decoding: A Pilot Study
papers.theme: ML for Neuroimaging, Neuroscience and Beyond
papers.abstract:
Closed-loop lower-limb exoskeleton control via Electroencephalography (EEG) remains limited by motion artifacts, low signal-to-noise ratio, and binary gait formulations that fail to capture full cortical gait complexity. We propose a 2-block Brain-Computer Interface (BCI) architecture: a trainable session-specific Feature Extraction Block with real-time artifact suppression and 
multi-domain feature extraction, coupled with a Decoder Block built on a novel Polynomial Time-Varying Layer (PolyTVL)+LSTM for four-state gait classification (Stand, Initiate, Execute, Terminate). Ablation confirmed $v01$ (PolyTVL+LSTM) outperformed all variants (validation MCC: 0.435, gap: 0.187), with consistent EEG feature discriminability across ROIs and sub-bands ($p<0.05$). Closed-loop deployment with $v01$ achieved 55.3\% (Rex-assisted) and 52.7\% (volitional) gait initiation success, with a mean end-to-end processing time of 70.5 ms ($\pm$41.5), validating real-time feasibility in this pilot study.

papers.title: BAT-CLIP: Trimodal Alignment of Brain, Audio and Text
papers.theme: ML for Neuroimaging, Neuroscience and Beyond
papers.abstract:
Decoding and interpreting naturalistic speech from the brain increasingly relies on alignment to pretrained speech and language representation spaces. However, current CLIP-style brain–speech alignment ground neural activity to a single anchor modality—audio or text—despite the brain’s inherently multimodal speech processing. This induces a trade-off: audio anchoring preserves temporal structure but weakens linguistic separability, while text anchoring captures semantics yet discards acoustic detail.
We propose $\textbf{\emph{BAT-CLIP}}$, the first CLIP-style trimodal alignment framework for iEEG that jointly aligns neural embeddings to both pretrained audio and text anchors in a shared, frozen audio–text manifold. On the naturalistic Podcast benchmark, $\textit{BAT-CLIP}$ yields more robust representations than bimodal CLIP baselines. We also highlight the importance of using self-supervised foundation models for CLIP training.

papers.title: COGNITIVETWIN: ROBUST MULTI-MODAL DIGITAL TWINS FOR PREDICTING COGNITIVE DECLINE IN ALZHEIMER'S DISEASE
papers.theme: ML for Neuroimaging, Neuroscience and Beyond
papers.abstract: Predicting individual cognitive decline in Alzheimer's disease requires high accuracy, demographic fairness, and robustness to missing data. We present CognitiveTwin, a digital twin framework that forecasts patient-specific cognitive trajectories. The model integrates multi-modal longitudinal data (clinical, imaging, biomarker, and genetic) using a Transformer-based fusion architecture coupled with a Deep Markov Model for temporal dynamics. Evaluated on 1,666 patients from the TADPOLE dataset, CognitiveTwin predicted 24-month Mini-Mental State Examination (MMSE) scores with a Mean Absolute Error (MAE) of 1.619 and a progression AUROC of 0.912. The model achieved uniform calibration (Expected Calibration Error = 0.054), strict performance parity across biological sex and age groups, and degraded by only 0.3\% under a simulated 15\% missing-not-at-random (MNAR) scenario. Ablation studies confirm the critical necessity of both temporal modeling and multi-modal fusion. CognitiveTwin provides accurate, equitable, and resilient forecasting for personalized care planning and clinical trial enrichment. Code is available at \url{https://anonymous.4open.science/r/cognitivedt-FF2A}.

papers.title: Graph-Constrained Hawkes Modeling of EEG Seizure Propagation
papers.theme: ML for Neuroimaging, Neuroscience and Beyond
papers.abstract: Many dynamical systems, including brain networks, generate activity that propagates across interacting entities over time. Multivariate Hawkes process is a powerful tool for modeling such event-driven dynamic systems. However, learning fully dense interactions usually leads to noisy and non-interpretable event propagation structure. In this work, we study how sparse graph priors can guide temporal propagation learning through graph-constrained Hawkes modeling. The proposed framework restricts event dynamics to graph structured pathways, leading to more structured and interpretable event-propagation estimates. We evaluate the approach on EEG seizure propagation modeling using multichannel scalp EEG recordings from the CHB-MIT dataset. Experimental results show improved held-out likelihood and next-node propagation prediction compared to unstructured Hawkes baselines. These findings suggest that incorporating graph structure can improve continuous-time propagation modeling in multivariate event systems.

papers.title: HYPERGRAPH-BASED HIGHER-ORDER INTERACTION MODELING FOR DYNAMIC COGNITIVE LOAD ESTIMATION USING SINGLE-CHANNEL FNIRS
papers.theme: ML for Neuroimaging, Neuroscience and Beyond
papers.abstract: Cognitive load estimation using functional near-infrared spectroscopy (fNIRS) has gained increasing attention in human centered and neuroergonomic applications. However, existing approaches often rely on multi-channel recordings and conventional feature representations, which fail to capture higher-order temporal and contextual relationships. To address these limitations, this work introduces hypergraph based higher-order interaction (HOI) modeling for dynamic cognitive load estimation using a single-channel fNIRS signal. Multi-domain features extracted from oxyhemoglobin (HbO) and difference hemoglobin (HbS) signals are used to model hypergraphs capturing temporal, feature-similarity, class-level, and subject-specific relationships. Data were recorded from 15 healthy participants under baseline (B), low cognitive load (LCL), and high cognitive load (HCL) conditions. Hypergraph-derived features were combined with conventional features and evaluated using FastRNN, FastGRNN, Light-weight Recurrent Network (LRN), and Temporal Convolutional Network (TCN) models under Leave-One-Subject Out (LOSO) cross-validation. The combined feature representation consistently outperformed individual feature sets, with TCN achieving accuracies of 78.50% for 3-class classification, 99.71% for B vs LCL, and 87.83% for B vs HCL classification. SHAP-based explainability analysis further demonstrated that hypergraph-derived features provide complementary discriminative information for model decision making. The experimental findings highlighted the potential of hypergraph-based HOI modeling to compensate for limited spatial information and support subject-independent cognitive load estimation using a compact single-channel fNIRS system.

papers.title: INTER-SUBJECT SCREENING FRAMEWORK OF MYOCARDIAL INFARCTION DETECTION USING CNN FROM VECTORCARDIOGRAM SIGNALS
papers.theme: ML for Neuroimaging, Neuroscience and Beyond
papers.abstract: Accurate detection of myocardial infarction (MI) from cardiac bio-signals remains challenging, particularly when models are required to generalize to unseen subjects. Most vectorcardiogram (VCG)-based methods reported in the literature are evaluated under intra-subject or beat-level cross-validation settings, which may lead to optimistic performance estimates. To address this issue, a convolutional neural network (CNN)-based framework is proposed for inter-subject MI detection using VCG bio-signals. The model incorporates a learnable lead-identity embedding to capture lead-specific characteristics while enabling shared learning across the three orthogonal VCG leads. The approach is evaluated on the Physikalisch--Technische Bundesanstalt Diagnostic Database using subject-independent VCG beats. The joint model achieves an overall Matthews correlation coefficient (MCC) of 63.66\% on the complete unseen test set. Lead-wise evaluation further shows that the jointly trained model achieves its highest performance on the $V_y$-filtered test subset, with an MCC of 72.53\%. These results demonstrate the potential of lead-flexible VCG-based deep learning for MI screening under strict inter-subject evaluation.

papers.title: LISTEN: ADAPTIVE LOW-SEPARATION-RANK RIDGE REGRESSION FOR TENSOR COVARIATES
papers.theme: ML for Neuroimaging, Neuroscience and Beyond
papers.abstract:
Modern applications increasingly generate tensor-structured data (i.e., multiway arrays), which are often used as covariates in regression problems. In this work, we focus on ridge regression with tensor covariates, where a common approach is to vectorize each tensor and estimate an unstructured coefficient vector. However, this approach fails to exploit the tensor structure of the regression coefficients and can create high-dimensional, ill-posed estimation problems when sample sizes are limited. Prior work has addressed these challenges by imposing low-separation-rank (LSR) structure on the coefficient tensor, thereby reducing the effective complexity of the model.
However, existing factorized LSR methods require the separation rank to be specified a priori, making model selection computationally expensive and the resulting estimator sensitive to rank misspecification. We propose LISTEN, an implicitly regularized LSR-structured ridge regression framework that enforces structure via a convex regularizer rather than an explicit rank-constrained factorization. We develop an alternating minimization algorithm with ADMM-based updates and establish a stationarity guarantee under exact block minimization. 
Synthetic experiments show that LISTEN adapts as the coefficient tensor deviates from a compact LSR structure, while neuroimaging experiments demonstrate competitive predictive performance relative to the considered baselines.

papers.title: Mechanistic-Interpretability Sparse Autoencoders for Mammalian Visual Cortex
papers.theme: ML for Neuroimaging, Neuroscience and Beyond
papers.abstract: Two-photon calcium imaging records hundreds of cortical neurons simultaneously across natural stimuli, yet how that population activity decomposes into interpretable, crosscontext-stable units remains opaque: principal components mix stimulus contexts into single high-variance modes, tuning curves do not scale beyond a few conditions, and contrastive latent embeddings are dense and polysemantic. The cortical population is itself polysemantic—each high-variance direction mixes multiple stimulus contexts—and the right tool to factorise it is an overcomplete sparse decomposition that yields units that are monosemantic and causally testable. We develop the corticalcalcium machinery and tests required to make such a decomposition actually answer neuroscience questions on Allen Brain Observatory data (the same family of methods has independently become the dominant interpretability tool for large language models, but the cortical population code is the problem we target). We build a calcium-aware top-K sparse autoencoder—preencoder bias, auxiliary-K dead-feature revival, and a GCaMP6ftuned temporal-smoothness term—and add three test tools: a cross-paradigm firing-rate-rank consistency (cp) score that measures how stably each feature’s activation rank survives switching stimulus paradigm; a condition-axis permutation null that makes the cross-mouse alignment test non-degenerate; and a per-frame variance lower bound that any mean-pool encoder must obey, escaped by a frame-wise SAE. On 30 Allen Brain Observatory sessions spanning 6 visual cortical areas and 4 excitatory cre lines, SAE features beat PCA on cp in 30 of 30 sessions (p = 9.3×10−10 , Cohen’s d = +1.98; the 30/30 win holds within every cre line individually), simultaneously beat ICA / vanilla AE / CEBRATime on 28/30, and beat an LFADS sequential VAE on 4/6 matched-session evaluation. Causally ablating top-cp features drops cp more than ablating random controls (specificity +0.107, 6/6 sessions); a hierarchical layer-2 SAE lifts cp where layer1 has slack (18/22 non-ceiling sessions win, p = 1.3 × 10−3 ); SAE features universalise across animals on 4/8 paradigmoverlapping cross-mouse pairs (Z > 2); and the frame-wise variant recovers +0.37 to +0.60 per-frame FVE on 10 sessions while a matched LFADS-lite mean-pool baseline collapses to ≈ 0, independently confirming the variance bound. Applied as a discovery tool, the SAE surfaces three cortical predictions: a cell-class signature in which L2/3 (Cux2) over-represents naturalscenes-preferring features and L4 (Rorb / Scnn1a / Nr5a1) overrepresents drifting-gratings-preferring features (Fisher p = 0.017 and 0.007); a paradigm-breadth gradient that tracks the Harris et al. mouse-visual-area hierarchy (Spearman ρ = +0.71); and a 9-entry per-(area, cre-line) atlas of named features in which each entry lists the Allen session id, feature index, preferred stimulus, and top-5 driving neurons—the first SAE-derived candidatemicrocircuit predictions on cortical calcium imaging, and a falsifiable target list for follow-up recording and perturbation. Code under MIT

papers.title: Mixture-of-Experts Subspace Fusion in Multimodal Latent Brain Network Representation Learning
papers.theme: ML for Neuroimaging, Neuroscience and Beyond
papers.abstract: Neurodegenerative diseases such as Alzheimer’s disease (AD) involve complementary functional and structural brain alterations that are difficult to capture using single-modality neuroimaging models. While multimodal variational autoencoders (MMVAEs) have shown promise for integrating fMRI and sMRI data, existing fusion strategies typically rely on global latent integration, limiting their ability to model heterogeneous modality contributions across latent factors. To address this limitation, we propose a Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) subspace fusion framework for multimodal variational representation learning for brain networks. The proposed model partitions the latent space into multiple subspaces and independently learns adaptive modality weights within each partition using probabilistic gating. Experiments on the ADNI dataset demonstrate that the proposed subspace fusion improves latent representation quality, identifies disease-discriminative latent subspaces, and exhibits robustness to missing modalities through adaptive gate compensation without requiring retraining.

papers.title: MSR-IVA: A State-Aware Framework for Structural MRI and Dynamic Functional Connectivity
papers.theme: ML for Neuroimaging, Neuroscience and Beyond
papers.abstract: Multimodal fusion of structural MRI (sMRI) and dynamic functional network connectivity (dFNC) can reveal how brain structure relates to changing functional states. When the same structural latent representation is coupled with multiple states, applying independent vector analysis (IVA) separately to each state can produce unrelated structural decompositions, while forcing identical decompositions may suppress state-specific relationships. In addition, not every subject expresses every dynamic state. We propose masked structural residual IVA (MSR-IVA), a state-aware framework that combines a shared structural representation with state-specific residual adaptations and masks for incomplete state expression. On an Alzheimer's Disease Neuroimaging Initiative cohort, MSR-IVA improved matched source coupling by 6.5% and reduced unmatched dependence by 15.7% relative to the independent pairwise IVA baseline. Among subjects expressing both states, mean absolute cross-state structural source correlation was 0.9177 for MSR-IVA versus 0.2978 for no sharing, demonstrating controlled structural sharing that preserves source correspondence while allowing state-specific adaptation.

papers.title: Network analysis of High Frequency Oscillations to differentiate resective surgery outcome
papers.theme: ML for Neuroimaging, Neuroscience and Beyond
papers.abstract: High frequency oscillations are a promising biomarker of epileptic tissue and have the potential to improve patient outcomes in resective epilepsy surgery. However, analysis of HFO rate alone has not led to improvement in seizure freedom rates post-resective surgery. This, and epilepsy's nature as a network disorder, have driven the need for interpretable network analysis of HFOs. Our objective was twofold: 1) to develop a methodological pipeline that reveals the network context of HFOs at their moment of generation and 2) to assess our method's clinical relevance. We found that at the moment of interictal HFO generation, out-degree, in-degree, and CheiRank centralities differ in the seizure onset zone, compared to the rest of the network, such that seizure free patients are statistically differentiable from non-seizure free patients.

papers.title: Network Instability Spectrum Characterizes Altered Topographic Dynamics in Schizophrenia
papers.theme: ML for Neuroimaging, Neuroscience and Beyond
papers.abstract:
Dynamic functional connectivity studies typically
quantify time-varying coupling among predefined networks,
while temporal variation in network spatial topography is less
often characterized. Here, we introduce the Network
Instability Spectrum, a frequency-domain framework for
quantifying how window-wise spatial instability of intrinsic
connectivity networks fluctuates over time. For each subject
and network, we computed a topographic instability
trajectory as the dissimilarity between each window-specific
spatial map and the subject-specific mean map, then extracted
spectral features from this trajectory. Using resting-state
fMRI from 160 healthy controls and 151 individuals with
schizophrenia, we found network-specific group differences,
with the largest number of FDR-significant effects observed
for mean instability and low-frequency instability power.
Nested cross-validation showed that NIS features contained
diagnosis-relevant information, with tree-based models
achieving AUC values around 0.76–0.77 and balanced
accuracy around 0.70. A label-permutation test confirmed
statistically significant above-chance classification. These
findings suggest that schizophrenia is associated with altered
temporal organization of intrinsic network topographies and
that NIS provides an interpretable complement to
conventional dynamic connectivity analysis.

papers.title: P300 Transfer to Spelling Decisions: A Strict bigP3BCI Benchmark
papers.theme: ML for Neuroimaging, Neuroscience and Beyond
papers.abstract: P300 spellers enable assistive communication, yet weak single-flash responses, calibration burden, and cross-study variation limit deployment. We develop a strict transfer benchmark on bigP3BCI, a multi-study EDF+ corpus of online P300 speller recordings, with a MOABB-derived P300 4L export as a secondary stress test. We extract stimulus-locked epochs and speller illumination masks from BCI2000 state channels and evaluate xDAWN-LDA, temporal logistic regression, and xDAWN-Riemannian baselines under random, subject-held, and leave-one-study-out splits. On a six-study subset with 225,124 epochs from 240 EDF files, the strongest baseline reaches 0.651 AUC under subject holdout; leave-one-study-out AUC ranges from 0.548 on StudyN to 0.712 on StudyR. Offline character accumulation reaches 0.308 accuracy under subject holdout and 0.073–0.521 across held-out studies under an up-to-96-flash budget. Pooled epoch-level summaries can obscure target-study spelling failures. The MOABB export remains near chance under strict splits, motivating export validation before cross-corpus claims.

papers.title: Plug-and-Play PET Reconstruction with Learned Flow-Matching Priors
papers.theme: ML for Neuroimaging, Neuroscience and Beyond
papers.abstract: Positron emission tomography (PET) is a powerful functional imaging technique, but image reconstruction from low-count PET data remains a challenging Poisson inverse problem. In this work, we introduce a novel plug-and-play (PnP) PET reconstruction framework that incorporates a learned flow-matching generative prior. This prior induces a deterministic transport-based denoiser through a flow-matching ordinary differential equation (ODE). We embed this denoiser within an alternating direction method of multipliers (ADMM) optimization scheme. The proposed method alternates between a Poisson-specific data-consistency step, implemented via an expectation-maximization (EM)-type update, and a transport-based denoising step driven by the flow-matching ODE. Numerical experiments demonstrate that the proposed method achieves superior reconstruction quality compared with conventional iterative methods and state-of-the-art deep learning baselines, while maintaining high computational efficiency.

papers.title: STATIC AND DYNAMIC BRAIN CONNECTIVITY PATTERNS ACROSS SLEEP DURATION
papers.theme: ML for Neuroimaging, Neuroscience and Beyond
papers.abstract:
Sleep duration is associated with brain health, but it remains
unclear whether short and long sleep are related to simi-
lar or distinct patterns of intrinsic brain connectivity. We
analyzed resting-state fMRI data from 14,021 UK Biobank
participants and examined static functional network connec-
tivity (sFNC) and dynamic functional network connectivity
(dFNC) across three sleep-duration groups: short (≤6 h),
normal (7–8 h), and long (≥9 h). After adjustment for de-
mographic, imaging, lifestyle, and health-related covariates,
269 of 1,378 sFNC connections were significantly associated
with sleep duration after Bonferroni correction. These associ-
ations were distributed across multiple large-scale networks,
with prominent involvement of subcortical, sensorimotor, vi-
sual, cognitive-control, default-mode, and cerebellar systems.
Pairwise group comparisons showed the largest number of
significant sFNC differences between long and short sleep-
ers. Dynamic analyses identified three recurring connectivity
states. Longer sleep duration was associated with greater
occupancy of States 1 and 3 and lower occupancy of State
2, with significant differences across sleep-duration groups.
Together, these findings suggest that sleep duration is related
to both distributed differences in average functional connec-
tivity and systematic shifts in the temporal expression of
recurring brain-connectivity states.

papers.title: UMPIRE-Net: Unrolled Magnitude-Phase Regularization Network for Accelerated MRI
papers.theme: ML for Neuroimaging, Neuroscience and Beyond
papers.abstract: MRI reconstruction from undersampled k-space measurements is an ill-posed inverse problem. Physics-driven deep learning (PD-DL) methods have shown strong performance for this task by combining the MRI forward model with learned image regularization within algorithm-unrolling frameworks. However, most existing PD-DL methods reconstruct complex-valued images directly, thereby implicitly coupling magnitude and phase within a single learned representation. This coupled regularization may be suboptimal in reconstruction settings where accurate phase modeling plays an important role, such as partial Fourier (PF) imaging, where recovery of the omitted asymmetric k-space measurements depends on the underlying image phase. In such scenarios, explicit modeling of magnitude and phase as separate components may reduce the reliance on externally estimated or predefined phase information. To this end, we propose UMPIRE-Net (Unrolled Magnitude-Phase In REgularization Network), a PD-DL method that introduces separate learned regularizers for magnitude and phase components, together with a novel data-fidelity formulation that enforces measurements consistency. We evaluate UMPIRE-Net for accelerated MRI with PF across different datasets and acceleration factors. Experimental results demonstrate that our proposed method improves reconstruction quality compared with a conventional complex-valued PD-DL baseline, yielding sharper images and reduced artifacts.

papers.title: BEAT-SYNCHRONOUS TOKENIZATION FOR ECG TRANSFORMERS
papers.abstract: Transformer-based electrocardiogram (ECG) models commonly tokenize waveforms into fixed temporal patches. Though convenient, fixed patching can split heartbeat structures across token boundaries. We study beat-synchronous tokenization as a physiologically grounded alternative, comparing fixed patches with three beat-aligned strategies: resampled beats, adaptive pooled beats, and resampled beats augmented with R–R interval information. Experiments span two settings: 10-second 12-lead diagnostic classification on PTB-XL after MIMIC-IV-ECG masked pretraining, and 60-second single-lead rhythm classification on Icentia11k after patient-level contrastive pretraining. On PTB-XL, resampled beat tokens achieve the highest mean macro Area Under the ROC Curve (AUROC; 0.8945) and nearly match the best fixed-patch macro Area Under the Precision-Recall Curve (AUPRC; 0.7414), reducing average sequence length from 100 to 11.2 tokens. On Icentia11k, beat-synchronous tokenizers obtain comparable AUPRC to fixed patching with better stability across runs. These results suggest morphology-preserving beat tokenization is a compact, competitive alternative to fixed temporal patching.

papers.title: Delays in Spiking Neural Networks: A State Space Model Approach
papers.abstract: Spiking neural networks (SNNs) are biologically inspired, event-driven models suited for temporal data processing and energy-efficient neuromorphic computing. In SNNs, richer neuronal dynamic allows capturing more complex temporal dependencies, with delays playing a crucial role by allowing past inputs to directly influence present spiking behavior. We propose a general framework for incorporating delays into SNNs through  additional state variables. The proposed mechanism enables each neuron to access a finite temporal input history. The framework is agnostic to neuron models and hence can be seamlessly integrated into standard spiking neuron models such as Leaky Integrate-and-Fire (LIF) and Adaptive LIF (adLIF). We analyze how the duration of the delays and the learnable parameters associated with them affect the performance. We investigate the trade-offs in the network architecture due to additional state variables introduced by the delay mechanism. Experiments on the Spiking Heidelberg Digits (SHD) dataset show that the proposed mechanism matches existing delay-based SNNs in performance while remaining computationally efficient, with particular gains in smaller networks.

papers.title: DYLNC: DYNAMICS-AWARE LATENT NETWORK COMPONENT DECOMPOSITION FOR TEMPORAL NETWORKS
papers.abstract: Temporal networks often evolve through recurring structural patterns whose activations change over time. A key challenge is to recover these connectivity  patterns while also explaining how their activations progress across time. In this paper, we propose a dynamics-aware latent network decomposition that represents each graph snapshot as a linear combination of latent network components with time-varying coefficients. Unlike decomposition-only approaches that treat temporal coefficients as free variables or impose only smoothness priors, the proposed formulation jointly learns the latent components, coefficient trajectories, and a low-dimensional progression rule. To capture the deviations not explained by autonomous evolution, we include a learned exogenous forcing term and impose multi-step consistency for stable long-term dynamics. Experiments on synthetic and real temporal network data show that the proposed model recovers interpretable latent network components while capturing temporal evolution.

papers.title: EARLY FUSION-BASED LEARNING OF MULTI-CHANNEL EMG SIGNALS FOR MUSICAL FINGER PRESS RECOGNITION
papers.abstract:
Real-time detection of exact finger-press events on musical
keyboards is expected to enable appropriate corrective
actions in the early stages of a student’s learning. Surface
EMG (sEMG) signals capture the spatio-temporal characteristics
of musculoskeletal activity triggered by finger-press
events. In this study, sEMG signals are used to identify
finger-press actions that produce musical notes.Features were
extracted from signals recorded using eight MyoBand electrodes
positioned circumferentially around the forearm to
comprehensively capture the underlying muscle activity corresponding
to finger-press events. However, it is challenging
to spatially distinguish the events from the individual electrodes
of the Myoband placed around the forearm. Hence,
in this work an early fusion approach is proposed using
classifiers on 8-electrode EMG signals acquired around the
forearm to better decode finger-press movements even with
a low sampling rate of 200Hz. Recognizing the finger press
event within the span of the recorded window is further enhanced
by detecting sEMG activity that represents the onset
& offset of the signal. This work proposes an early fusion of
Electrode features extracted from the end-pointed signal by
correlating them with the simultaneously captured Musical
Instrument Digital Interface (MIDI) signal over the recorded
span, which represents the real EMG activity due to finger
movement. Features extracted from MIDI Gated End Pointed
Signals post early fusion are classified by Random Forest
(RF) and Deep Neural Network (DNN) models. The best
classification accuracy of RF - 90.39% and DNN - 92.98%
was achieved for 5 fingers to generate distinct musical notes

papers.title: Frequency-Adaptive Auditory Frontend for Microphone-Domain Sound Event Localization and Detection
papers.abstract: Microphone-domain sound event localization and detection (SELD) commonly combines log-mel and GCC-PHAT features to represent spectral and spatial information. However, this fixed fusion ignores that their reliability can vary across frequency regions. This paper proposes FAAF, a Frequency-Adaptive Auditory Frontend that dynamically weights log-mel and GCC-PHAT branches using signal-dependent gating and an auditory-inspired frequency prior. The resulting weights are applied inside feature extraction, enabling backend-agnostic spectral-spatial cue integration. Experiments on the STARSS23 dev-test split show consistent improvements over the conventional mel+GCC frontend with both ResNet-Conformer and CST-Former backends, reducing SELD scores by up to 3.76\% and 2.23\%, respectively. Analysis of learned weights reveals an interpretable transition around 1.5~kHz, suggesting that FAAF learns frequency-dependent cue allocation aligned with spatial hearing.

papers.title: High resolution projected contactless capacitive sensing through hardware support and AI super resolution
papers.abstract:
Projected non-contact capacitive sensor arrays (CSAs) provide spatial measurements of electric fields but are limited by hardware-constrained resolution and noise. This work investigates whether learning-based super-resolution (SR) can recover high-resolution spatial structure from low-resolution, noisy CSA measurements. Formulating this as a spatial signal reconstruction problem, we construct a synchronized multimodal dataset pairing CSA data with video-based heatmaps for supervision. We develop a multiscale vision transformer (ViT) model utilizing both spatial and temporal data for $8\times 8\rightarrow 16\times 16$ and  $16\times 16\rightarrow 32\times 32$ reconstruction tasks.
Our model outperforms bilinear and bicubic baselines, improving peak signal-to-noise ratio by up to 2.72 dB and structural similarity index (SSIM) by 6.52\% relative to the bilinear baseline. We also demonstrate a cross-modality training paradigm using vision data to train CSAs without requiring higher-density sensor hardware. Our results suggest that SR effectively increases CSA resolution, offering a pathway to improved inference in human activity recognition systems.

papers.title: Human-in-the-Loop Active Learning for Rare Poultry Vocalization Discovery in Long-Term Farm Recordings
papers.abstract: Monitoring poultry welfare in large-scale farming environments requires reliable detection of vocalizations associated with disturbance, stress, and other welfare-relevant states. However, rare calls such as the bukbuk-bukak (BKK) vocalization occur infrequently in long-term barn recordings, making manual discovery time-consuming. This study presents an active-learning framework for rare-vocalization discovery and dataset expansion in a research cage-free layer facility. Starting from 116 manually verified BKK events, a Random Forest classifier with handcrafted acoustic features was trained to screen continuous barn recordings. Candidate detections were reviewed through a human-in-the-loop process, where confirmed BKK events were added as positives and acoustically similar false detections were retained as hard negatives near the decision boundary. Across only three screening rounds, the framework expanded the verified BKK dataset from 116 to 587 events, a 5-fold increase, while collecting 446 hard negatives. Screening precision improved from 36.7% to 72.5%, showing that iterative retraining with boundary hard negatives improved discovery efficiency. The expanded dataset enabled comparison of RF with CNN, Vision Transformer, and wav2vec+MLP detectors, with the CNN achieving the best held-out performance with an F1 score of 0.89. These results suggest that human-in-the-loop active learning with hard-negative mining can efficiently bootstrap rare vocalization datasets from long-term recordings and support acoustic poultry welfare monitoring.

papers.title: Label-Informed Multiple Imputation for Time Series with Missing Data
papers.abstract: Missing data are common in time series and present a challenge for downstream learning, as most machine learning models---including those adapted for temporal structure---require complete inputs. In this paper, we address missingness in time series extrinsic regression (TSER), where each series is paired with a continuous label external to the observed sequence. To this end, we propose a label-informed multiple imputation framework based on Geometry- and Accuracy-Preserving (GAP) proximities extracted from supervised, tree-based time series models, producing imputations that align with downstream predictive objectives rather than relying solely on unsupervised reconstruction. The resulting procedure uses training labels during imputation and naturally extends to external, unlabeled datasets. We demonstrate improvements in downstream predictive performance under controlled missingness across TSER benchmarks, and we provide an expanded TSER benchmark that includes modern tree-based models not previously evaluated.
