papers.title: Mitigating Over-Suppression in Speech Enhancement via Inference-Time Rethink-and-Refine Correction Module
papers.abstract: We present a rethink-and-refine correction module that addresses over-suppression, a common failure mode of speech enhancement (SE) models, where speech cues are suppressed alongside noise. Our method operates entirely in the inference stage without additional training, allowing seamless integration with diverse SE models. Given noisy and enhanced signals, we obtain word- or phoneme-level alignments using an automatic speech recognition model and identify intervals where enhancement is unreliable. These intervals are then selectively remixed through convex interpolation, with per-segment weights optimized to maximize a composite objective balancing perceptual quality and speech preservation. Experiments on the URGENT 2024 and 2025, VCTK-DEMAND, and MSP-PODCAST datasets show consistent improvements in perceptual quality, intelligibility, and downstream performance compared to conventional SE alone, demonstrating the benefit of rethink-and-refine framework for robust speech processing.

papers.title: Optimal Transport with Frequency Warping for Bags of Spectra
papers.abstract: This paper introduces optimal transport algorithms for the case of probability distributions over normalized frequency spectra with frequency warping. Signals and random processes are statistically characterized as mixture distributions over normalized spectra as descriptors for locally stationary processes. Practically, a signal or process is represented by a bag of spectra, an empirical distribution on a set of normalized spectra taken from short-time windows or random realizations, respectively. Calculating the optimal transport between two spectral mixtures involves the underlying distance between the spectra supporting the mixtures and the optimization of the transport plan. Motivated by biosignal applications where the physiological processes of individuals may operate at different time scales, we consider the optimal transport between processes that may have a similar spectral signature but exhibit a monotonic `warping' of the frequencies. We incorporate the search over monotonic functions of frequency, which changes the distance metric between spectra, as part of the optimal transport problem. On a benchmark time-series classification dataset, we verify that the optimal transport between bag of spectra creates a metric space that is superior for k-nearest neighbor compared to using a single spectra per time-series. We demonstrate proof-of-concept of the proposed optimal transport with time warping between vocal audio tracks of individual singers.

papers.title: Probabilistic Load Forecasting from Limited Client Data using Gaussian Processes and Kalman Filtering
papers.abstract: Real-time probabilistic load forecasting is essential for efficient energy management. Predicting the total electrical load of, for example, an energy community or microgrid typically requires metering all clients, which is costly and raises privacy concerns. This paper proposes a method for probabilistic load forecasting using real-time measurements from a limited subset of clients. The approach models each client's time-varying share of the total load as a Gaussian process, trained on historical aggregate data. A Kalman filter then sequentially estimates the total load in real-time using only the subset of client measurements. The method is evaluated on a real-world residential load dataset consisting of 54 clients. The results indicate that the prediction error decreases sublinearly with both the number of observed clients and the amount of training data, and accurate and calibrated one-step-ahead forecasting of the total load is achievable with only a small fraction of clients and as little as 7 days of half-hourly historical training data.

papers.title: QSMP: finding representative time series subsequences through Quick Shift + Matrix Profile
papers.abstract: Finding representative waveforms in long time series has scientific and practical value in many domains, as it enables summarization and visualization of large time series datasets, and downstream tasks like classification and forecasting. We present here QSMP, a method to find representative waveforms in long time series through a density-guided clustering of time series subsequences. Our method makes a novel connection between Quick Shift, a mode-seeking algorithm, and the Matrix Profile, a time series similarity-search data structure, to adapt Quick Shift to the clustering of subsequences in long time series, with a time and space complexity that is superior to the state-of-the-art method. Our experiments on synthetic and real datasets show that QSMP can be a valuable tool to summarize and visualize long time series by finding representative waveforms.

papers.title: RADAR SIGNAL DETECTION AND LOCALIZATION IN SHARED SPECTRUM USING DEEP OBJECT DETECTORS
papers.abstract: Reliable incumbent-radar sensing enables dynamic spectrum sharing in the 3.5~GHz Citizens Broadband Radio Service (CBRS) band, where missed detections delay incumbent protection. We formulate sensing as object detection on time--frequency spectrograms of NIST CBRS I/Q records. We compare YOLO one-stage detectors with DETR-family detectors, and compressed full-record inputs with overlapping time-axis tiles. Among the detectors evaluated, the best convolutional model (YOLOv8m) and the best transformer model (DINO-DETR) show no statistically significant difference. Because sensing requirements are specified by class-specific detection probability at a bounded false-alarm rate, aggregate metrics are insufficient. Evaluated at comparable realized false-alarm probabilities, tiled inference yields a 3.8-point detection-probability advantage for DINO-DETR, yet no configuration reaches 0.99 across all evaluated SNRs. Operational evaluation should therefore report missed-detection and false-alarm behavior with class- and SNR-specific results, rather than aggregate metrics such as mAP alone.

papers.title: ROBUST STATE-SPACE RECONSTRUCTION OF BRAIN DYNAMICS VIA BOOTSTRAP MONTE CARLO SSA
papers.abstract: Reconstructing latent state-space geometry from time series provides a powerful route to studying nonlinear dynamics across complex systems. Delay-coordinate embedding provides the theoretical basis but assumes long, noise-free recordings, which many domains violate. In many real-world domains, recordings are short, noisy, and coarsely sampled; in neuroimaging, for example, fMRI additionally contains autocorrelated background structure that can obscure oscillatory components and destabilize embeddings. We propose bootstrap Monte Carlo singular spectrum analysis (BMC-SSA), which combines Monte Carlo SSA with bootstrap stability to retain oscillatory modes that are statistically supported and reproducible across resampled data. This produces reconstructions that emphasize reliable oscillatory structure, enhancing determinism and stabilizing subsequent embeddings. Our results show that BMC-SSA improves the reliability of functional measures and uncovers differences in state-space dynamics in fMRI, offering a general framework for robust embedding of noisy, finite signals.

papers.title: Subspace Learning with Interval-Censored Likelihoods for Dequantizing Percept™ PC LFP Snapshots
papers.abstract: Implanted neurostimulators that sense local field potentials now enable chronic electrophysiology based biomarker tracking in patients at home. The Medtronic Percept™ PC, the only commercially available sensing-enabled deep brain stimulation (DBS) device, stores spectral amplitudes as 16-bit integers at approximately $0.1\,\mu$V per bit (quantum $q \approx 0.11\,\mu$Vp). At frequencies where the true amplitude spans only a few quantization levels, consecutive bins round to the same stored value. Standard spectral parameterization (FOOOF, fitting oscillations and one over f), which separates periodic peaks from the aperiodic $1/f$ activity, treats every value as exact and fits oscillatory peaks to these plateaus. Because these spectra feed clinical biomarker pipelines and spectral foundation models for symptom decoding, spurious peaks can corrupt downstream inference. Across 9{,}438 spectra from 14 hemispheres in 7 subcallosal cingulate DBS patients, 20.6\% of peaks detected at [2\,45] Hz have no match in ground truth synthesized by quantizing clean in-clinic BrainSense™ recordings, while aggregate beta band power and the aperiodic exponent are preserved. We formalize dequantization as interval-censored subspace estimation and compare five classes of correction methods. Quantized probabilistic PCA is the only tested method that reduces the spurious rate (20.6\% to 18.3\%) while preserving true peak detection and keeping noise floor RMSE below $q/\sqrt{12}$.

papers.title: Time-Warping Estimation via Stationarity-Based Learning of the De-Warped Signal
papers.abstract: Time-warping estimation is a fundamental problem in signal processing with applications in bioacoustics, radar, and biomedical analysis. This paper introduces a Time-Warping Estimation Trainable (TWET) model for estimating time-warping functions from a single observation. The proposed approach formulates time-warping estimation as a stationarization problem in the wavelet domain and leverages a hierarchical dilated convolutional architecture to estimate the time-warping functions. A differentiable stationarity criterion is introduced for end-to-end optimization. TWET is compared with existing approaches. Experimental results show improved deformation reconstruction accuracy together with significantly reduced computation time, making the framework compatible with low-latency applications.

papers.title: TYPE INFERENCE ON STRIPPED BINARIES USING HYPERGRAPH NEURAL NETWORKS
papers.abstract: As binary executables are compiled into stripped binaries, information about these types is lost forever. Although state-of-the-art binary type inference techniques such as TYGR use Graph Neural Networks (GNN) to infer types based on control flow graphs and data flow graphs, traditional graphs fail to efficiently represent multiple occurrences of the same type without sacrificing contextual accuracy. In this extended abstract, we propose a forward-thinking approach for moving binary type inference from traditional pairwise graphs to hypergraphs. We show that although using traditional graphs with the Clique Expansion approach to efficiently represent hyperedges is plagued with catastrophic message passing noise, constructing a Hypergraph Neural Network using a Relational Graph Attention Network (RGAT) architecture mathematically solves the problem. Our preliminary results using a subset of 1,000 binaries show that our approach is able to achieve an accuracy of 68.86\%, which is greater than the accuracy of the traditional RGCN approach at 65.59\%.

papers.title: Unsupervised learning of Kalman prediction-update steps using neural networks
papers.abstract: This paper presents an algorithm for learning the prediction or the update step of a Kalman filter in nonlinear systems via neural networks in an unsupervised manner. In the update step, the algorithm learns to perform statistical linear regression with respect to the predicted density. This is achieved with an efficient architecture in which a neural network is used to predict the measurement, and the required linearisation matrix is obtained by applying backpropagation to the same neural network. In the prediction step, the network predicts the mean and the covariance matrix of the state. Experimental results demonstrate the benefits of the proposed networks.

papers.title: A Semi-Parametric Framework for Open Vocabulary Panoptic Segmentation
papers.abstract:
Open vocabulary panoptic segmentation aims to jointly predict semantic categories and instance masks for arbitrary user-specified concepts, including categories not observed during training. Existing approaches are predominantly parametric, relying on classifier weights learned from fixed segmentation vocabularies. As a result, their performance deteriorates significantly when transferring to unseen categories and out-of-distribution domains. In this work, we propose SPPS (Semi-Parametric Panoptic Segmentation), a semi-parametric framework that augments parametric segmentation models with an external segment-level visual memory. 

Specifically, we construct a large-scale memory database of masked segment representations from paired image-text data using open-vocabulary object detection and segmentation. During inference, masked segment features extracted from the query image are used to retrieve semantically similar segment exemplars from the memory. The retrieved neighbors induce a non-parametric classifier via similarity-weighted voting, while a parametric classifier derived from CLIP-based segmentation provides complementary category predictions. The proposed formulation enables scalable open vocabulary segmentation through memory expansion without requiring retraining for new categories. When trained on COCO and evaluated on ADE20k, SPPS achieves 30.9 PQ, 19.3 mAP, and 44.0 mIoU, improving over the parametric baseline by +4.5 PQ, +2.5 mAP, and +10.0 mIoU, respectively.

papers.title: Bridging Vision and Language — A Multi-Image AI Pipeline for Context-Aware NPC Storytelling
papers.abstract:
The landscape of interactive media and video games has evolved from simple, linear progression into expansive, open-world environments where player agency dictates the flow of events. As rendering technologies and physics engines have advanced to create highly realistic simulations, the systems governing in-game storytelling have often lagged behind. In most contemporary open-world games, Non-Playable Character (NPC) dialogue remains heavily pre-scripted. While branching dialogue trees offer the illusion of choice, they are ultimately finite and struggle to account for the emergent, unpredictable actions players take in a physics-driven world.

We have a three stage pipeline where video game footage is sampled, objects
in the frame are identified, and the sequence of frames are turned into
a summary of the gameplay, as if the summarizer is an NPC in the game.
The proposed architecture separates visual perception from narrative generation to strictly ground the AI in gameplay reality. First, a VLM sequentially processes in-game images to extract key entities, actions, and environmental states, structuring this data into a chronological scene graph. Second, a Large Language Model (LLM) utilizes this structured data to generate dramatically meaningful and credible NPC dialogue.

To evaluate the game-play summaries, we primarily rely on LLM's.
We found the summaries are typically good, with lack of repetition and lack of arbitrary content among the best categories.
Results suggest that LLM-based judges overestimate emotional quality and, to a lesser extent, engagement.

papers.title: C2A: COUPLING SPATIAL EVIDENCE WITH CLINICAL PRIORS VIA CO-OCCURRENCE AWARE CLASS ATTENTION FOR MULTI-LABEL CHEST X-RAY CLASSIFICATION
papers.abstract: Thoracic pathologies rarely occur in isolation, yet standard multi-label classifiers rely on shared global descriptors, discarding *where* findings lie and *how* they co-occur. We propose **C$\mathbf{^2}$A** (Co-occurrence Aware Class Attention), a classification head that explicitly couples spatial evidence with clinical priors. First, C$^2$A casts pooling as an expectation over learned per-class spatial attention maps, yielding localized descriptors for each disease. Second, it couples these descriptors via a learnable graph warm-started from empirical label co-occurrence. A single residual message-passing step shares evidence among related findings, proving to be a bounded perturbation of the identity where co-occurrence enters each logit through an explicit bilinear interaction. On CheXpert, C$^2$A achieves a superior $0.895$ macro-mean AUROC, outperforming advanced context-gating baselines. Crucially, gains concentrate on highly co-occurrent classes with ambiguous spatial evidence (rescuing Atelectasis by $+1.5$ over GCG), demonstrating the prior's regularizing effect with a negligible overhead of one linear projection and a $C\times C$ edge matrix.

papers.title: DISENTANGLING CO-OCCURRING RETINAL PATHOLOGIES WITH SALIENCY-GUIDED SPARSE EXPERT ROUTING
papers.abstract: Retinal fundus images frequently exhibit multiple co-occurring pathologies, yet standard deep learning classifiers apply static, identical computation to every image regardless of the underlying disease distribution. We propose a novel architecture that resolves this via sparse conditional computation, pairing a Guided Context Gating (GCG) spatial attention front-end with a sparsely-routed Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) block operating over feature tokens. Crucially, this routing yields an interpretable, data-driven decomposition. Expert allocation is significantly disease-dependent ($p < 0.001$), with the healthy "Normal" state and morphologically distinct pathologies (e.g., ERM, AMD) isolating to dedicated experts. On a five-class, patient-disjoint 5-fold cross-validation benchmark, our model achieves $0.912 \pm 0.008$ macro AUC and $0.653 \pm 0.014$ macro F1. Furthermore, Grad-CAM++ and post-MoE t-SNE visualizations confirm that expert routing aligns with localized lesions and geometrically maps co-occurring cases between their constituent clusters, positioning sparse MoE as an interpretable approach to multi-disease retinal screening.

papers.title: Fully Decentralized Cooperative Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning Under Model Uncertainty
papers.abstract: Fully decentralized cooperative multi-agent reinforcement learning (MARL) requires agents to learn and act without centralized coordination or communication, using only the underlying state and their own actions. This setting is intrinsically difficult because each agent must treat the others as part of an unknown, non-stationary environment. The challenge is further amplified under model uncertainty, where transition dynamics may differ from the nominal model due to limited data, noise, or training-deployment mismatch. In this paper, we develop a robust learning framework for fully decentralized cooperative MARL under transition uncertainty. We introduce $(s,\mathbf{a})$-rectangular uncertainty sets and define a robust best-possible operator whose unique fixed point characterizes the best worst-case team performance achievable from each local action. Under a product-structure condition on robust optimal joint actions, we prove that independent greedy action selection recovers a robust optimal joint policy. We further design a monotone update that preserves convergence while avoiding explicit maximization over other agents' actions. The resulting algorithm, Robust Best-Possible Q-Learning (RBQL), stands for the first fully decentralized robust MARL with global optimality and convergence guarantee.

papers.title: Multimodal vs. Multi-View Transformer Fusion: A Robustness Benchmark for Robotic Arm Action Recognition
papers.abstract:
Which sensing strategy degrades more gracefully under 
real-world signal degradation: heterogeneous multimodal 
fusion or homogeneous multi-view redundancy? We present 
a systematic benchmark on RoboMNIST using Transformer-based 
architectures evaluated under progressive data incompleteness 
(10%-50%). Two findings emerge: multimodal fusion retains 
about 85% accuracy at 50% incompleteness versus 64% for 
multi-view; and despite three encoders, the multimodal model 
is more efficient in FLOPs and latency, as WiFi CSI and 
audio are computationally lighter than video. These results 
provide concrete guidelines for resilient robotic perception 
system design.

papers.title: Semantic Guided Stratified Sampling for Mitigating Visual Hallucinations
papers.abstract: Visual hallucination (VH) in Large Vision-Language Models (LVLMs) often arises from biases or semantic imbalance in the training data, where certain visual concepts are underrepresented. Existing mitigation strategies mostly rely on model-level alignment or instruction tuning, while the role of data selection has received relatively little attention. In this study, we introduce Classification-Based Stratified Sampling (CBSS), a sampling method that leverages semantic similarity between images and textual subject categories to construct semantic pairs without modifying model architecture or training objectives. Unlike standard sampling methods, CBSS assigns each image to one or more semantic groups and selects samples proportionally, ensuring that rare or underrepresented semantic concepts remain represented in the sampled evaluation subsets. We evaluate CBSS on the YNQ (Yes-No Question) visual hallucination benchmark and show reductions in hallucination frequency, achieving up to +8.5\% absolute improvement across different sampling scales. Our findings show that semantic-aware data selection can reduce the observed hallucination frequency in sampled evaluation subsets, particularly in smaller and intermediate sampling scales, demonstrating improvements across diverse evaluation conditions.

papers.title: Small Language Model enabled Autonomous agent for Language-Conditioned Cognitive Radar
papers.abstract: Modern radar systems require adapting their processing strategies in response to changing interference, clutter, and data availability. This paper introduces a framework for a small language model (SLM)-driven autonomous agent designed for language-conditioned cognitive radar, functioning as an intelligent controller for a suite of array signal processing tools. Given a natural-language command, the agent extracts radar-operation-related cues, selects an appropriate sequence of signal-processing methods, configures parameters, and invokes executable tools for numerical computation. Experiments with a synthetic uniform linear array (ULA) radar demonstrate that, given a natural-language command, the agent performs meaningful algorithm selection across diverse scenarios for sidelobe control, jammer suppression, multiple-null beamforming, coherent-source handling, and low-snapshot direction-of-arrival (DOA) estimation. Ablation results show that radar-specific prompting and physics-grounded tool execution are both required for reliable decisions and hallucination-free numerical results.

papers.title: Speculative Macro Commit for Faster Tool-Using Agents
papers.abstract:
Tool-using LLM agents spend wall-clock time not only on model inference but also in serial action--observation turns, where each tool call, environment transition, and observation can block the next decision. 
We introduce \textbf{Speculative Macro Commit} (SMC), a runtime mechanism for a two-tier agent setting: a large authoritative actor model produces the official trajectory, while a faster speculative drafter model continuously predicts and executes future action chains on an isolated environment snapshot.
SMC mines recurring multi-action skeletons from training traces and uses them as runtime macro library for matching the fast drafter predicted action chain.
When the actor's next tool call matches the first drafted action, SMC can commit the remaining pre-executed draft steps, together with their observations, as official trajectory progress.
With Qwen3.5-27B INT4 as the authoritative actor model and Qwen3.5-4B as the speculative drafter model, SMC matches the sequential agent's overall accuracy while reducing latency by 10.23\% over the speculative actions baseline and 18.59\% over sequential execution on the $\tau^2$-Bench Telecom subset. 
On AppWorld, SMC reduces wall time by 7.7\% over speculative actions baseline and 44.9\% over sequential execution, with a small task-completion tradeoff. 
These results show that latent runtime macros can turn speculative agent work into end-to-end latency gains without sacrificing the overall performance.

papers.title: Structured State Reconstruction from Balatro Footage for Imitation Learning
papers.abstract: Expert demonstrations are valuable for imitation learning, but many commercial games do not provide structured logs, replay files, or APIs for querying environment state. This paper presents a video-based state reconstruction pipeline that converts public gameplay footage of the roguelike deck-building game Balatro into state-action trajectories: sequences of reconstructed game states paired with the actions the player took. The pipeline combines OCR, object detection for overlapping or modular objects, object tracking, zone-based grouping, persistent state parsing, and rule-based event detection to recover the game state and the player action at each decision point. Across 124 gameplay videos, the system reconstructs 735,288 tensorized decision steps from 1,973 gameplay runs and achieves a pooled event-extraction F1 score of 0.880 on manually annotated clips. We further train a branched behavioral-cloning policy on the reconstructed dataset, obtaining 70.4% family top-1 accuracy and 94.7% family top-3 accuracy on held-out test videos. These results show that ordinary gameplay video can be transformed into large-scale imitation-learning data without direct access to game-engine state, while highlighting structured action prediction and long-horizon decision making as remaining challenges.

papers.title: Uncertainty-Aware Agentic LLMs for Forensic Triage of Windows Event-Log Streams
papers.abstract:
Windows Event Logs are sparse, symbolic timestamped signals used during incident response, but manual triage
is slow when records are noisy and distributed across providers.
This paper presents an audit-oriented large language model
(LLM) pipeline for forensic event-log signal triage. The system
converts EVTX records into structured temporal windows, applies
carry-forward summarization, and uses three domain-specialist
LLM agents plus a Judge model to produce a final incident
narrative. Unlike single-response summarizers, each specialist
emits a structured claim envelope containing the primary activity
class, severity, actors, evidence identifiers, and MITRE ATT&CK
techniques. These envelopes make model disagreement measurable.
On five public Windows attack-log samples covering credential
access, lateral movement, persistence, and execution, the specialist
panel reached Fleiss’ κ = 0.352 for primary category labels but
κ = −0.286 for technique presence. The Judge matched the
expected primary category in four of five cases (80%, Wilson 95%
CI: 37.6–96.4%). Mean technique precision, recall, and F1 were
0.383, 0.367, and 0.349. A secondary runtime analysis showed 244.4
seconds of model time for 30 events, with an exploratory fit of 29.9
seconds fixed overhead plus 3.16 seconds per event. The results
show that local LLMs can accelerate first-pass forensic narrative
construction, but disagreement, weak technique calibration, and
small-sample uncertainty require human review.

papers.title: A Single-Parameter Factor-Graph Image Prior
papers.abstract:
We propose a novel piecewise smooth image model 
with spatially varying local parameters that are automatically 
adapted to each image.
Technically, the model is formulated in terms
of factor graphs with NUP (normal with unknown parameters) priors, 
and the pertinent computations amount to iterations of conjugate-gradient steps 
and Gaussian message passing.
The proposed model and algorithms are demonstrated 
with applications to denoising and contrast enhancement.

papers.title: Knowledge-Guided Pattern Discovery via Coupled Tensor Factorizations
papers.abstract: In order to understand complex systems such as the human metabolome or human brain, different sensing technologies are used, generating complex data. These datasets are often multiway, i.e., with more than two axes of variation such as a _subjects_ by _metabolites_ by _time_ array. While tensor factorizations have successfully revealed interpretable patterns from such complex data, they have so far been mainly data-driven. On the other hand, there is more to data -- there are computational models (of these systems), which are rich sources of prior information. In this paper, we introduce a knowledge-guided approach that brings together data and computational models by jointly analyzing real data and simulated data (generated using a computational model) using coupled tensor factorizations with linear coupling. Our experiments on real metabolomics measurements demonstrate that guiding the analysis of such noisy data with simulated data improves the pattern discovery performance while also revealing potential discrepancies between data and computational models.

papers.title: On the Convergence Speed-Accuracy Trade-Off in Competing Network Learning
papers.abstract: In this work, we study a stochastic two-team competition problem, where each team consists of a network of collaborating agents. Recent works have extended diffusion learning algorithms to this setting, including the adapt-then-combine and infer-then-combine (ATC-ITC) strategy, which employs a local inference step, and the competing diffusion (CD) strategy, which omits it. Although both methods have been shown to converge to an $\mathcal{O}(\mu)$-neighborhood of the Nash equilibrium, existing analyses do not clearly characterize their relative advantages. To address this gap, we develop a unified framework for refined analysis of CD and ATC-ITC through a controlled inference step. The resulting performance bounds reveal a fundamental trade-off: the inference step in ATC-ITC accelerates convergence but introduces persistent gradient noise that can degrade steady-state performance relative to CD. This insight motivates a time-varying inference mechanism to balance the trade-off. Simulations validate the theoretical findings and the effectiveness of the proposed strategy.

papers.title: Pheno-GS: Phenoscape-scale Geodesic Sinkhorn
papers.abstract:
High throughput single cell data is now being collected on entire cohorts of data, for example cancer patients. In order to understand such heterogeneity at a patient level from data that is at the cellular level, a new concept called phenoscaping is appearing. A phenoscape is a lower dimensional embedding, where each ”datapoint” is an entire single cell distribution, and distances between datapoint are optimal transport distances. For creating phenoscapes, computing geometry-aware OT at this large scale (between all pairs of patient datasets) remains an open challenge. Existing methods either rely on Euclidean ground metrics that distort intrinsic manifold structure or fail when data is sparse, unevenly sampled, or large in scale. We present Pheno-GS (Phenoscape-scale Geodesic Sinkhorn), a manifold OT system that computes accurate, scalable geodesic transport distances under noisy, unbalanced, and large-scale settings. Pheno-GS combines three core capabilities: 1) a graph connectivity regularization module that guarantees well-defined geodesic distances on sparse or disconnected manifolds; 2) an unbalanced OT formulation supporting transport between distributions of differing total mass via KL marginal penalties, and 3) a batched matrix algorithm that computes the full pairwise distance matrix with exactly two heat diffusions –
achieving over 200× speedup for 500 distributions compared to traditional Geodesic Sinkhorn. We validate Pheno-GS on synthetic manifold benchmarks and a high-dimensional single-cell CyTOF perturbation dataset, demonstrating superior geometric fidelity, robustness, and scalability over existing methods.

papers.title: TENSOR-NETWORK QUANTUM-INSPIRED SUCCESSIVE SUBSPACE LEARNING
papers.abstract: Successive subspace learning (SSL) constructs feedforward representations by learning local covariance eigenspaces. This paper develops tensor-network quantum-inspired successive subspace learning (TN-QiSSL), a density-operator analogue of SSL. Each normalized local patch is mapped to a quantum-inspired product state, the patch ensemble is summarized by an empirical density operator, and local features are obtained from its eigenspace through signed projection, projection-energy, and class-fidelity channels. The resulting layer keeps the stage-wise SSL pipeline but changes the geometry from Euclidean covariance to Hilbert-space density operators. The induced fidelity kernel is locally RBF-like, while tensor-network compression supplies a separate bond-dimension control for interaction complexity. Experiments on high-order interaction, synthetic texture, and KTH-TIPS2-b material recognition show that local TN-QiSSL improves over raw-patch, PCA/SSL, product-state, and sample-level variants when class information is carried by repeated local or high-order patch structure.

papers.title: Transistor-Level Energy Analysis of Signal Processing Algorithms: Beyond Operation Counting
papers.abstract:
Energy estimates for signal processing algorithms usually rest on
floating-point operation counts, which ignore memory traffic, com-
mand overhead, and the gap between textbook formulas and library
implementations. We present an energy model based on Transistor
Operations (TOs), the physics-grounded cost unit of the TOML
framework, and validate it on 37 signal processing algorithms in 8
categories on two NVIDIA GPUs (RTX 4090 and A100 SXM4). Its
four fitted coefficients (compute, memory, GPU-command dispatch,
fused-sequential step) take measured inputs: analytical operation
counts checked against Nsight Compute instruction counts, and per-
invocation GPU command counts measured with Nsight Systems. It
predicts energy with median errors of 26.6% and 19.9%, places 78%
and 73% of configurations within a factor of two, and ranks 82%
of head-to-head algorithm pairs correctly (75% under leave-one-
algorithm-out cross-validation). Profiling confirms the split-radix
FFT and 4-FMA complex MAC corrections and shows that library
kernels on tiny matrices execute 30 to 500 times the arithmetic
count as fixed work per launch. The per-command cost is set by
the host (233.8 vs. 29.5 μJ), which sets the payoff of kernel fusion;
sequential algorithms are 10 to 100× more energy-efficient on CPU;
and measured energy per operation spans 60× across floating-point
kernels, which bounds any constant-cost-per-operation model.

papers.title: WHEN DOES CONDITION INFORMATION HELP? AN EMPIRICAL ANALYSIS OF CONDITION-AWARE NORMALITY MODELING FOR NORMAL-ONLY ANOMALOUS SOUND DETECTION
papers.abstract: In normal-only anomalous sound detection (ASD), metadata can define distinct normal reference populations. We analyze condition-aware normality modeling at the scoring stage using frozen representations and normal training data only. Global Mahalanobis distance (MD), condition-wise MD, and rank calibration are compared on a controlled split of the DCASE 2024 Task 2 development data. Condition-wise MD improves area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC) over global MD for Audio Spectrogram Transformer (AST), WavLM, Hidden-Unit BERT (HuBERT), and BEATs; for AST, AUC increases from $0.5644$ to $0.6880$ and $0.6886$ after calibration. Diagnostics show condition structure and global-score bias in AST. Label perturbation, sample-size, covariance, and machine-wise analyses show dependence on condition-reference alignment, normal support, and representation geometry. Gains are larger for full AUC than low-false-positive pAUC, indicating that condition information can help as a reference-selection mechanism but is not universally beneficial.

papers.title: ALAS: AN AUTOMATIC LATENT ALIGNMENT SCORE FOR AUDIO LANGUAGE MODELS
papers.abstract: Large Language Models (LLMs) are extended into Speech-LLMs, and the quality of the audio-text alignment they learn affects most downstream Spoken Language Understanding (SLU) behavior. Yet despite a growth of fusion strategies, there is no standard way to measure how well a Speech-LLM internally binds audio frames to text tokens. We introduce ALAS (Automatic Latent Alignment Score), a model- and task-agnostic metric that probes the LLM's per-layer hidden states, scoring the cross-modal cosine similarity between audio and text representations against a Whisper-derived reference. ALAS needs only a frozen forward pass and an off-the-shelf ASR reference, with no training or fitted classifier, and is calibrated to an interpretable uniform baseline comparable across tasks. Applying ALAS to four open-source Speech-LLMs (AF3, Qwen2-Audio, Qwen-Omni, SALMONN) across emotion recognition (IEMOCAP), open-ended SQA (LibriSQA), and multi-choice audio understanding (MMAU-speech), we find that the depth and strength of alignment reflect each model's audio-encoder design and the acoustic-versus-semantic demands of the task, and that ALAS tracks but does not duplicate task accuracy, exposing models that score well without genuinely grounding in the audio. We release ALAS as an open-source library so that practitioners can probe their own Speech-LLMs or try new tasks.

papers.title: ATTENTION IS ALL YOU NEED FOR RF FINGERPRINTING: TRANSFORMER MODELS FOR SPECIFIC EMITTER IDENTIFICATION OF COMMERCIAL NAVIGATION RADARS
papers.abstract:
Specific Emitter Identification (SEI) is a key capability of  Electronic Surveillance (ES) systems. SEI attributes received signals to individual transmitters using unique fingerprints that arise from idiosyncratic, unintentional modulations imparted on pulses due to variations in transmitter hardware.

Prior approaches have looked at architectures such as CNNs and ResNets, however these incur high computational costs as model complexity increases, and are limited at capturing long-range dependencies efficiently. In this paper, a hybrid transformer encoder architecture is introduced, combining a convolutional layer for patch embedding with a transformer encoder for sequence modelling.

Results show the proposed architecture outperforms ResNet and Inception models of similar size on a dataset of commercial navigation radars collected in an anechoic chamber. The measured F1 score across radar range modes and SNRs indicates that all models exceed random guessing down to -5 dB SNR, with the transformer achieving up to 65.4% relative increase over the baseline at 0 db SNR.

papers.title: CARD: CALIBRATION-AWARE ROUTING FOR DOMAIN-AGNOSTIC INCREMENTAL AUDIO CLASSIFICATION
papers.abstract:
Domain-Incremental Learning (DIL) for audio classification requires models to adapt to new acoustic domains while preserving performance on previously learned ones. Many DIL systems use domain-specific layers or classifier heads, and are often evaluated in a domain-aware setting where the test-time domain identity is available. In practice, however, deployed audio systems may receive only an input signal without a reliable city, device, or recording-condition label, making inference-time head routing a key bottleneck.

We formulate domain-agnostic incremental inference as a calibration-sensitive routing problem and propose Calibration-Aware Routing for Domain-agnostic incremental audio classification (CARD). CARD is a training-free inference-time method that computes a routing score from confidence, margin, and entropy after temperature scaling. Because all heads share the same label space, CARD uses the routing score for either hard head selection or soft head mixture at the logit or probability level.

On 5-domain, 5-fold city-domain protocols constructed from TAU Urban Acoustic Scenes 2019 and TAU Urban Acoustic Scenes 2020 Mobile, CARD soft mixture achieves higher mean accuracy and better predictive calibration than standard hard-routing rules. On TAU2019, CARD soft prob reduces the gap to the domain-aware single-head reference to 1.58 percentage points, suggesting that calibrated multi-head evidence fusion is an effective inference-time strategy when the test-time domain identity is unavailable.

papers.title: In-Context Learning for Non-Stationary MIMO Equalization
papers.abstract: Channel equalization is fundamental for mitigating distortions such as frequency-selective fading and inter-symbol interference. Unlike standard supervised learning approaches that require costly retraining or fine-tuning for each new task, in-context learning (ICL) adapts to new channels at inference time with only a few examples. However, existing ICL-based equalizers are primarily developed for and evaluated on static channels within the context window. Indeed, to our knowledge, prior principled analyses and theoretical studies of ICL focus exclusively on the stationary setting, where the function remains fixed within the context. In this paper, we investigate the ability of ICL to address non-stationary problems through the lens of time-varying channel equalization. We employ a principled framework for designing efficient attention mechanisms with improved adaptivity in non-stationary tasks, leveraging algorithms from adaptive signal processing to guide better designs. For example, new attention variants can be derived from the Least Mean Square (LMS) adaptive algorithm, a multi-step gradient updates for improved long-term tracking(Multi-LMS) or Least Root Mean Square (LRMS) formulation for enhanced robustness. Experimental results demonstrate that ICL holds strong promise for non-stationary MIMO equalization, and that attention mechanisms inspired by classical adaptive algorithms can substantially enhance adaptability and performance in dynamic environments. Our findings may provide critical insights for developing next-generation wireless foundation models with stronger adaptability and robustness.

papers.title: LeAudioJEPA: Generic Audio Representation Learning for Identifying Whales in Cocktail Parties
papers.abstract:
Acoustic individual identification of sperm whales usually relies on temporal Inter-Pulse Intervals (IPI). In this work, we investigate whether sperm whale coda sequences could also encode discriminative information about speaker identity. 
To address this question, we introduce LeAudioJEPA, an audio adaptation of LeJEPA based on self-supervised learning of predictive latent representations. The model is pre-trained on AudioSet and evaluated on a sperm whale coda dataset collected off Mauritius between 2015 and 2024, including both mono-speaker and multi-speaker contexts involving three identified individuals.
We compare LeAudioJEPA with AudioJEPA, as well as supervised MLP, CNN, and ViT baselines trained from scratch, on a multi-label speaker classification task using Mel spectrograms. Results show that LeAudioJEPA achieves the best average macro-F1 score across full, mono-speaker, and multi-speaker test conditions over 20 seeds. Statistical testing over the 20 paired random seeds confirms that LeAudioJEPA significantly outperforms all evaluated trained baselines after FDR correction.
These findings suggest that coda sequences contain exploitable temporal context information for individual recognition, and highlight the potential of predictive latent architectures for low-annotation bioacoustic analysis.

papers.title: MLP Ensemble Learning for Non-Linear Distortion Correction in Radar Receivers
papers.abstract: Radar receivers often include radio-frequency limiters that protect the analog-to-digital converter by clamping the signal within its operating voltage range. When driven into saturation, these limiters introduce nonlinear distortion that corrupts the received waveform and cannot be corrected by conventional linear inverse filters. We present an ensemble of multilayer perceptrons (MLPs) that learns to correct this distortion directly from paired hardware measurements, treating reconstruction as a sample-level supervised regression problem with a sliding-window input of length W = 16. Three MLP architectures, (64, 32), (128, 64, 32), and (256, 128, 64) hidden units, are trained with tanh activations and the Adam optimizer and combined by unweighted averaging. We further propose an envelope normalized mean absolute percentage error (Env-MAPE), computed via the Hilbert transform, as an evaluation metric suited to the time-varying amplitude of non-stationary radar pulses. On a dataset with 160k samples representing operational measurement conditions, the ensemble achieves R2 = 0.9950 and Env-MAPE = 4.65% in a chronological hold-out test set, confirmed by five-fold cross-validation with Env-MAPE = 4.27 ±0.19%, demonstrating that a simple feed-forward architecture with local temporal context is sufficient to invert the receiver transfer function in this setting.

papers.title: NeuroState: Gradient-Isolated Boundary Learning for Interpretable EEG Transformers
papers.abstract: Transformer-based electroencephalography (EEG) classifiers achieve strong accuracy but offer no structural account of *when* brain states change, which limits their use where transition timing guides clinical decisions. We introduce NeuroState, a multi-resolution EEG transformer whose auxiliary boundary module estimates changepoint probabilities that condition attention. Our central result is an optimization one. Across eleven controlled interventions we document *auxiliary head collapse*, a failure mode in which jointly trained boundary modules converge to near-constant outputs, and we show that the deciding factor is not the loss or the mask but the order in which gradients are allowed to flow. Attention-Contrastive Boundary Learning (ACBL) with gradient isolation, a three-phase curriculum that detaches boundary gradients from the classification path during a formation phase, is the only one of the eleven that yields non-degenerate boundaries. Over five seeds NeuroState attains Cohen's $\kappa = 0.596 \pm 0.018$ on Sleep-EDF staging and area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUROC) $0.924 \pm 0.014$ on CHB-MIT cross-subject seizure detection, with AUROC 0.913 on TUAB. A shuffled-input null shows that the Sleep-EDF boundaries carry measurable content in every seed, while conditional tests on CHB-MIT find no transition-related structure, so we present the accompanying concept-based and spectral analyses as preliminary and scope our conclusions to the EEG settings measured here.

papers.title: Online Bayesian Node Classification on Inductive Graphs under Distribution Shift
papers.abstract: On evolving graphs, node classifiers face two demands: inductive generalization to newly arriving nodes under distribution shift, and calibrated uncertainty for safety-sensitive applications. Standard graph neural networks (GNNs) are trained once and address neither. We adapt the Bayesian last layer (BLL) model, placing {\it random} last-layer (LL) parameters atop a {\it deterministic} GNN encoder for uncertainty quantification. The categorical softmax likelihood needed for classification breaks Gaussian conjugacy, so neither the training posterior nor the test-time streaming update admits a closed-form solution. We address both: a variational Bayesian last layer (VBLL) objective jointly trains the encoder and an approximate LL posterior by maximizing an evidence lower bound with Monte-Carlo expected log-likelihood; at test time, an online Laplace update on the LL posterior (encoder frozen) amounts to a power-prior Bayesian model with exponential forgetting and a Kullback-Leibler (KL) anchor to the training posterior. Across five node classification benchmarks under distribution shift, the online VBLL is the only model to win both accuracy and NLL on every dataset, with gains up to $+17$ points on \texttt{Cora} and $+14$ points on \texttt{ogbn-arxiv} over the strongest non-VBLL baseline, and remains competitive on calibration against MC Dropout, Deep Ensembles, Temperature Scaling, and Gaussian-process classifiers.

papers.title: Operating-Conditioned Quantile Regression with Conformal Calibration for Adaptive Gearbox Vibration Thresholding
papers.abstract:
Fixed global thresholds ignore speed–load drift, whereas
regime-binned limits become unstable in sparsely sampled
operating cells. Quantile regression can model smooth context changes, but an uncalibrated quantile can trade high
detection for unacceptable false-alarm rate (FAR). Moreover,
calibrating 18 condition indicators (CIs) separately before
OR and persistence logic does not calibrate the deployed
alarm. We propose post-fusion conformal calibration of
operating-conditioned quantile residuals. Eighteen vibrationonly CIs are robustly normalized, fused by a regularized
Mahalanobis score, and causally median-filtered; one splitconformal threshold is fitted to this final score. On five locked
PHM 2023 splits, the method obtains 1.05% FAR and 82.17%
detection rate, versus 21.58% and 88.12% for per-CI OCQR–
CC. On all 1,006 Ferrara acquisitions, it gives 4/58 false
alarms and 135/135 late-life detections. Feature-to-alarm
latency is 9.21 ms on an Intel i7-11800H CPU

papers.title: PARTIAL DISCHARGE DETECTION IN COVERED CONDUCTORS USING A MULTI-SCALE CNN-BILSTM MODEL WITH BRANCH ATTENTION
papers.abstract: Medium-voltage (MV) overhead distribution systems traditionally employ bare conductors, which are vulnerable to vegetation-related faults due to the lack of external insulation. Covered conductors (CCs) reduce direct conductor-to-vegetation contact and improve reliability, but they introduce high-impedance faults (HIFs) that are difficult to detect using conventional protection methods. These faults are often associated with partial discharge (PD) activity, an indicator of insulation degradation. Existing PD detection methods often rely on handcrafted features, classical machine learning, or computationally expensive signal transformations. This paper proposes a Multi-Scale CNN-BiLSTM with Branch Attention (MS-CNN-BiLSTM) deep learning model for PD detection in MV overhead power lines. The proposed model combines one-dimensional convolutional feature extraction, multi-scale bidirectional LSTM branches, and branch attention to learn representations from minimally processed raw signals. Experimental results show that the model achieves an MCC of 0.63, F1-score of 0.77, accuracy of 0.82, precision of 0.76, and recall of 0.78.

papers.title: Spatiotemporal Analysis and Operating State Classification of a 10-MW Kaplan Turbine Generator using Machine Learning
papers.abstract: This study presents a spatiotemporal analysis and data-driven classification framework for operating-condition monitoring of a 10-MW Kaplan turbine generator. Synchronized air-gap flux-density measurements from ten stator-mounted Hall probes and rotor-current measurements from six channels are analyzed under seven steady-state guide vane opening (GVO) conditions. From 1s windows, spatial Fourier indicators, probe-resolved temporal flux features, and channel-wise RMS current features are extracted. Correlation analysis and principal component analysis are used to interpret feature-GVO relationships, while Random Forest, SVC-RBF, and multilayer perceptron classifiers are used for supervised GVO classification. Results show that rotor-current features primarily represent electrical loading, whereas flux-based features provide complementary information on spatial non-uniformity, temporal distortion, and low-frequency modulation. Spatial-only indicators are insufficient for reliable classification, with accuracies below 27\%, while current-only features provide a stronger baseline of approximately 84-85\%. The best performance is achieved by combining flux and current features, where the SVC-RBF classifier reaches 99.5\% test accuracy and macro-F1 score. These findings demonstrate that distributed magnetic sensing and rotor-current measurements provide complementary information for accurate data-driven monitoring of hydrogenerator operating conditions.

papers.title: TRAINING-FREE REAL-TIME MULTIMODAL CHANGE-POINT DETECTION WITH COVERAGE AND REALISM DIAGNOSTICS
papers.abstract: We present CoRe (Coverage-Realism Change-Point Detection), a training-free front end for multimodal change-point detection (CPD) and out-of-distribution (OOD) monitoring on frozen embedding streams. CoRe compares adjacent windows with a bounded directional kernel discrepancy whose coverage component measures missing nominal support and whose realism component measures unsupported current content. It applies the same directional statistic to adjacent-feature differences as a flux score, exposing order-only temporal changes that preserve marginal feature distributions. The result is a detector-compatible evidence stream with native post-alarm diagnostics. We evaluate CoRe on 12 video, audio, and time-series benchmarks against five scalar baseline families, temporalized variants, and support-sensitive attribution controls, complemented by ablations, sensitivity sweeps, OOD severity studies, and end-to-end timing. The results show that CoRe uniquely combines state-shift evidence, temporal-order sensitivity, coverage/realism attribution, degradation tracking, and real-time deployment: scalar distances, temporalized scores, and support-sensitive controls each cover part of this operating profile, but not all of it in one training-free CPD front end.

papers.title: Transfer Learning for Avian Bioacoustics under Sparse Positive Labels
papers.abstract: Passive acoustic monitoring is an important tool for biodiversity assessment and wildlife conservation because it supports continuous and non-invasive monitoring of species across large spatial and temporal scales. Robust monitoring remains challenging because many datasets contain sparse positive labels, where species presences may be confirmed while unannotated species cannot be assumed absent. In this work, we study transfer learning under sparse positive labels using BirdCLEF+ 2026 as a target benchmark and BirdCLEF 2021, iNatSounds, WABAD, and BirdSet as external bioacoustic sources. We introduce a multi-source reliability framework that models heterogeneous bioacoustic datasets as distinct supervision sources with differing reliability. Our approach achieves 0.584 macro average precision and 0.860 macro AUC on public BirdCLEF+ 2026 validation labels while outperforming naive source pooling strategies. The strongest gains arise from passive acoustic monitoring datasets and biologically informed source selection. Our findings suggest that transfer learning in bioacoustics is fundamentally a weak supervision and negative transfer problem.

papers.title: Using acoustics to track the growth in black soldier fly larvae
papers.abstract: Black Soldier Fly larvae (BSFL) convert organic waste into protein-rich biomass, making them valuable for sustainable waste management and livestock feed. Monitoring larval growth conventionally relies on manual weighing, which is labor-intensive and typically limited to daily measurements. As a non-intrusive alternative, we propose passive acoustic monitoring, using continuously measured substrate surface temperature as a proxy for larval metabolic activity and growth. We use deep learning to extract relevant acoustic features and predict surface temperature from acoustic recordings, evaluating a baseline convolutional neural network and an attention augmented variant across three growth cycles. Our results demonstrate that acoustic signals can reliably track BSFL growth.

papers.title: When Does Cross-Substation Transfer Work? A Measurement-Heterogeneity Diagnosis of Feeder Fault Localization on Real Distribution Data
papers.abstract:
Machine-learning feeder fault localization is accurate within a single
substation but rarely tested across substations. Using real
multi-substation field recordings from a North American electric
utility company, in-distribution localization accuracy is high ($92.3\%$), while naive single-source transfer to an unseen, measurement-anomalous
station is weak (at best $44.8\%$; chance $33.3\%$).
We diagnose the cause: the anomalous station references its
zero-sequence voltage on the ground-fault-neutralizer side, inverting
its baseline polarity by about $180^\circ$, and the per-station median
$|V_0|$ differs by a factor of about $24$ across stations. A
measurement-invariant representation with two pooled,
convention-compatible sources recovers low-impedance-fault transfer to
$58.4\%$, but source diversity is non-monotonic---pooling all five
sources is worse (negative transfer)---and invariant features hurt
convention-compatible targets. Adaptation is fault-type-dependent:
transfer suffices for low-impedance faults, whereas high-impedance
faults require locally labeled events.
